sentences.text: Ryan! Look who’s here!
sentences.note: - **Look who’s here!**: 이게 누구야?(친한 사람을 예상치 못한 장소에서 만났을 때 하는, 놀라움과 반가움을 동시에 나타내는 표현)

sentences.text: Good to see you. What a small world.
Long time no see. How have you been?
sentences.note:
- **Long time no see**: 오랜만이다
- **How have you been?**: 그동안 어떻게 지냈어?

sentences.text: I’m doing great. You haven’t changed a bit.
sentences.ko: 잘 지내고 있어. 넌 하나도 안 변했구나.
sentences.note:
- **be doing great**: 잘 지내고 있다
- **haven’t changed a bit**: 하나도 안 변했다

sentences.text: Nice talking to you. Say hello to your wife.
sentences.ko: 대화 즐거웠어. 와이프한테 안부 전해 줘.
sentences.note: - **say hello to** sb: ~ 에게 안부를 전하다

sentences.text: Catch you later. I’ll keep in touch.
sentences.note:
- **Catch you later**: 다음에 보자
- **keep in touch**: 연락하다

sentences.text: What do you like about spring?
sentences.note: - **What do you like about** sth/sb?: ~ 에 대해 뭐가 좋아?

sentences.text: A lot of trees burst into blossom all across the country.
sentences.note:
- **burst into blossom**: (꽃이) 만개하다
- **all across the country**: 전국적으로

sentences.text: Let’s check out the cherry blossom festival tomorrow.
sentences.ko: 내일 벚꽃 축제를 같이 보러 가자.
sentences.note:
- **check out** sth: ~ 를 보러 가다(가 보다)
- **cherry blossom festival**: 벚꽃 축제

sentences.text: Sure. We have to leave early to beat the traffic.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 일찍 출발해 교통 혼잡을 피하자.
sentences.note: - **beat the traffic**: 교통 혼잡을 피하다

sentences.text: I’ll call you first thing in the morning.
sentences.note: - **first thing in the morning**: 일어나자마자(출근하자마자)

sentences.text: I’ll pack a big lunch for us.
sentences.note: - **pack a** (big) **lunch**: 도시락을 (많이) 싸 오다

sentences.text: Do you have any seats available?
I'm afraid all flights are fully booked.
Hello, is this United Airlines?
I'd like to book a flight to LA.
I want to reserve a flight to London.
Are there any seats available?
How much is a ticket to LA?
Are there any seats left for Friday?
Do you have a direct flight to Sydney?
That flight is fully booked.
I'm sorry, but that flight is booked up.
All seats are booked for July.
Can I go standby?
Can you put me on the waiting list?
sentences.ko: 저를 대기자 명단에 올려 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: I got something for your birthday.
A present for me? You shouldn’t have!
sentences.note: - **You shouldn’t have!**: 이러지 않아도 되는데! | 뭐 이런 걸 다!

sentences.text: It’s cold outside. I’ll give you a ride home.
sentences.ko: 바깥 날씨가 추워. 집까지 태워 줄게.
sentences.note: - **give** sb **a ride**: ~ 를 태워 주다

sentences.text: Don’t bother, but thanks anyway.
sentences.ko: 일부러 그럴 거 없어, 어쨌든 고마워.

sentences.text: Don’t mention it. That’s what friends are for.
sentences.note:
- **Don’t mention it**: 천만에(상대방이 감사의 인사를 하면 '천만에요', '신경 쓰지 마세요'라고 응답할 때 사용하는 표현)
- **That’s what friends are for**: 친구 좋다는 게 뭐야

sentences.text: Something smells fishy. Just be yourself.
sentences.note:
- **Something smells fishy**: 수상한 냄새가 나다
- **be oneself**: 평소처럼 행동하다

sentences.text: The movie begins at 6. Let’s leave around 5.
sentences.note: - **around** 숫자: ~ 시경에

sentences.text: Okay. The traffic isn’t bad at that time of day.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 하루 중 그 시간에는 차가 안 막히니까.
sentences.note:
- **The traffic is** (so) **bad**: 차가 (많이) 막히다
- **at that time of day**: 하루 중 그 시간에는

sentences.text: I’ll pick you up from your place.
sentences.note: - **pick** sb **up from** 장소: ~ 를 ~ 로 데리러 가다

sentences.text: Thanks, but don’t go out of your way.
sentences.note: - **go out of** one’s **way**: 일부러 ~ 하다

sentences.text: No problem. It’s on my way to the cinema.
sentences.note:
- **No problem**: 괜찮아 | 물론이지
- **on** one's **way to** 장소: ~ 에 가는 길이다

sentences.text: Give me a call when you’re about to leave.
sentences.note: - **give** sb **a call**: ~ 에게 전화하다

sentences.text: What's your departure date?
I'd like to leave on the 10th of July.
When are you leaving?
When are you planning to leave?
When would you like to depart?
What's your return date?
When will you return?
When would you like to return?
What day will you be returning?
My return date is July 24th.
What's the departure time?
What's the arrival time?
Your flight will arrive at 10:30 a.m. local time.
sentences.ko: 탑승하신 비행기는 현지 시간으로 오전 10시 30분에 도착합니다.

sentences.text: Are you traveling alone?
No, I'm traveling with my family.
What’s the weather gonna be like this Saturday?
sentences.ko: 이번 주 토요일 날씨가 어떨 것 같아?
sentences.note: - **What’s** sb/sth **like?**: ~ 은 어때?('What + be-V ~ like?'는 사물이나 사람의 상태를 물을 때 사용하는 표현)

sentences.text: The weather reporter said it was gonna be raining.
I get the feeling that we should call off our trip.
sentences.ko: 여행을 취소해야 할 것 같다라는 느낌이 들어.
sentences.note:
- **get the feeling that** S V: ~ 하는 느낌이 들다
- **call off**: 취소하다

sentences.text: Boy! It totally slipped my mind.
sentences.note: - **It slipped** one’s **mind**: 깜빡 잊어버렸어

sentences.text: Don’t tell me you were going to go alone behind my back.
sentences.ko: 설마 나 몰래 혼자 가려고 했던 건 아니겠지.
sentences.note:
- **Don’t tell me** S V: 설마 ~ 하려는 건 아니겠지
- **behind** one's **back**: ~ 의 뒤에서 | ~ 몰래

sentences.text: No way. I’ll just go with the flow.
sentences.ko: 말도 안 돼. 난 그냥 대세를 따를 거야.
sentences.note: - **go with the flow**: 대세를 따르다

sentences.text: No more impulse buying! It’s been two hours.
sentences.note: - **impulse buying**: 충동 구매

sentences.text: Don’t be so pushy. I’m doing my best.
sentences.note:
- **pushy**: 강압적인
- **do** one’s (very) **best**: 최선을 다하다

sentences.text: Pretty please. Let’s just stick to our shopping list.
sentences.note: - **stick to** sth: ~ 에 충실하다

sentences.text: Would you stop it? Don’t try my patience.
sentences.note: - **try** one’s **patience**: 인내심을 시험하다

sentences.text: Let’s split up. I’ll go get some beers.
sentences.ko: 일단 흩어지자. 맥주를 좀 사러 갈게.
sentences.note:
- **split up**: 흩어지다
- **go get some** sth: ~을 사러(가지러) 가다

sentences.text: OK. I’ll see you at the cashier in 10 minutes.
sentences.note: - **I’ll see you at(in)** sth: ~ 에서 만납시다

sentences.text: One-way or round-trip?
Round-trip, please.
Which class would you like?
Economy class, please.
Business class, please.
First class, please.
One-way, please.
Do I have to change planes?
You'll have to change planes in Chicago.
Is there a non-stop flight?
Is there a layover?
You have a layover in Chicago.
How long is the layover?
You need to wait for one hour in New York.
I feel like going out with you tonight.
sentences.ko: 오늘 밤에 너랑 놀러 가고 싶어.
sentences.note: - **feel like** V-ing(N): ~ 하고 싶은 기분이다

sentences.text: I’m sorry, but I have a previous engagement.
Nothing beats beer with chicken on a hot day.
sentences.ko: 이렇게 더운 날엔 치맥보다 나은 게 없지.
sentences.note: - **Nothing beats** sth: ~ 만 한 것이 없다 | ~ 이 최고야

sentences.text: Come to think of it, I can’t miss a drinking session.
sentences.ko: 다시 생각해 보니, 내가 술자리를 놓치면 안 되지.

sentences.text: That’s it! You might as well cancel your appointment.
sentences.ko: 바로 그거야! 너 약속 취소하는 게 낫겠다.
sentences.note: - **might as well** V: (대안이 없을 때) ~ 하는 게 나을 것 같다

sentences.text: I’m gonna have to postpone it for another day.
sentences.note: - **postpone** sth **for another day**: 다른 날로 연기하다

sentences.text: What’s going on? Why do you eat like a bird?
sentences.note: - **eat like a bird**: 소식하다(아주 조금 먹다)

sentences.text: I’m getting overweight. I’m trying to cut down on carbs.
sentences.ko: 체중이 늘고 있어서. 탄수화물 섭취를 줄이려고 노력 중이야.
sentences.note:
- **get overweight**: 체중이 늘다
- **cut down on** V-ing(N): ~ 를 줄이다

sentences.text: I doubt you can do it. You’re a big fan of carbs.
sentences.ko: 네가 할 수 있을까? 너 탄수화물을 매우 좋아하잖아.
sentences.note:
- **I doubt** S V: ~ 못할 것 같은데
- **be a big fan of** sth: ~ 를 매우 좋아하다

sentences.text: Not any more. I have to watch my weight.
sentences.note: - **watch** one’s **weight**: 체중을 조절하다

sentences.text: I think you look good the way you are.
sentences.note: - **the way you are**: 있는 그대로

sentences.text: Don’t stop me. I have my heart set on doing it.
sentences.note:
- **Don’t stop me**: 말리지 마
- **have** one’s **heart set on** V-ing(N): ~ 하기로 결정하다

sentences.text: I'd like to confirm my reservation.
What's your reservation number?
I'd like to reconfirm my flight.
I'd like to change my reservation.
I'd like to cancel my reservation.
I'm calling to cancel my flight.
May I have your name and flight number?
Can I change the date for my flight?
I'd like to reschedule my flight.
I'd like to change it to May 18th.
Can I change to an earlier flight?
sentences.ko: 더 이른 항공편으로 변경할 수 있나요?

sentences.text: I'd like to leave one day later.
I'm calling to change my destination.
Do you know your reservation number?
Your flight is confirmed.
How did you get those plane tickets?
I pulled some strings. I have good connections.
sentences.ko: 내가 백을 썼지. 좋은 인맥이 있거든.
sentences.note:
- **pull some strings**: 연줄을 대다 | 백을 쓰다
- **have good connections**: 좋은 인맥이 있다

sentences.text: I knew it. Care for some coffee after lunch?
sentences.ko: 그럴 줄 알았어. 점심 먹고 커피 한잔 어때?
sentences.note: - (Would you) **care for** N?: ~ 좀 하실래요(드실래요)?(친한 사이에서 격식 없이 상대의 의향을 물을 때 사용하면 좋은 표현)

sentences.text: You’re a big fan of coffee. Go easy on it.
sentences.ko: 커피를 정말 좋아하는구나. 적당히 좀 마셔.
sentences.note:
- **be a big fan of** sb/sth: ~ 의 광팬이다 | ~ 을 좋아하다
- **go easy on** sth: ~을 적당히 하다

sentences.text: It’s not gonna kill you to have one.
sentences.ko: 한잔 마신다고 큰일 나는 거 아니잖아.
sentences.note: - **It’s not gonna kill you to** V: ~ 한다고 큰일 안 난다

sentences.text: Don’t forget to bring Anna.
sentences.note: - **Don’t forget to** V: ~ 하는 거 잊지마

sentences.text: Are you ready to go out for dinner?
sentences.note:
- **go out for** sth: ~ 을 하러(먹으러) 가다
- **be ready to** V: ~ 할 준비가 되다

sentences.text: Yes, but I’m feeling a bit bloated.
sentences.note: - **feel bloated**: (속이) 더부룩하다

sentences.text: Really? What have you had at lunch?
I think I ate some tteokbokki in the afternoon.
sentences.ko: 오후에 떡볶이를 좀 먹은 것 같아.
sentences.note: - **I think** S V: ~ 인 것 같다

sentences.text: Can I get you something to ease your stomach?
sentences.ko: 너에게 속을 편하게 해 줄 것을 사다줄까?
sentences.note:
- **get** sb **something**: ~ 에게 ~ 을 사다주다
- **ease** one’s **stomach**: 속을 편하게 하다

sentences.text: No, thanks. I’ll have some porridge delivered.
sentences.note: - **have** sth **delivered**: ~ 를 배달시키다

sentences.text: Check-in, please.
May I have your e-ticket and passport?
Where is the check-in counter for Korean Airlines?
Go down this way.
It's near the Gate 7.
I have booked my flight online.
Do you want a window seat or an aisle seat?
sentences.ko: 창가 쪽 좌석을 원하시나요, 통로 쪽 좌석을 원하시나요?

sentences.text: Window seat, please.
Aisle seat, please.
Do you have a seating preference?
I'd like to sit in the front.
Can I have a seat next to the emergency exit?
sentences.ko: 비상구 옆 좌석으로 앉을 수 있을까요?

sentences.text: I'd like two seats next to each other.
sentences.ko: 나란히 붙어 있는 좌석 두 개로 부탁합니다.

sentences.text: I'd like to sit with my company.
Sorry to keep you waiting. So where were we?
sentences.note: - **keep** sb **waiting**: ~ 를 기다리게 하다

sentences.text: We need to fix the date for the next meeting.
sentences.note: - **fix the date**: 날짜를 확정하다

sentences.text: When is the most convenient time for you?
sentences.note: - **When is the most convenient time?**: 언제가 가장 편하세요?

sentences.text: Too bad I’m not able to make time this week.
sentences.ko: 안타깝게도 이번 주는 시간을 낼 수가 없어요.
sentences.note:
- **make time**: 시간을 내다
- **Too bad** S V: ~ 라서 안타깝다

sentences.text: Try to look on the bright side.
sentences.note: - **look on the bright side**: 긍정적으로 생각하다(친구가 좋지 않은 일로 의기소침해 있을 때 격려의 말로 쓰면 좋은 표현)

sentences.text: Got it. Keep me posted on your progress.
sentences.ko: 알았어요. 진행 상황을 계속 알려 줘요.
sentences.note: - **keep** sb **posted**: (진행 상황을) 계속 알려 주다

sentences.text: Look at you! It looks like you got a perm.
sentences.note:
- **It looks like** S V: ~ 한 것 같다
- **get a perm**: 파마를 하다

sentences.text: Yes. Can you tell? How do I look?
sentences.note: - **tell**: 알아차리다(구별하다)

sentences.text: It looks great. You look younger than your age.
sentences.note: - **look younger than** one’s **age**: 나이보다 어려 보이다

sentences.text: Really? That’s what I’ve always wanted.
sentences.note: - **I’ve always wanted to** V: 난 늘 ~ 하길 원했어

sentences.text: You’re really into taking care of your looks.
sentences.ko: 너는 외모를 관리하는 것에 정말 관심이 많아.
sentences.note:
- **be into** V-ing(N): ~ 에 관심이 많다(좋아하다)
- **take care of** one’s **looks(appearance)**: 외모를 관리하다

sentences.text: I have a date tonight. I want to leave a good impression.
sentences.ko: 저녁에 데이트가 있어. 좋은 인상을 남겨야지.
sentences.note:
- **have a date** (with sb): ~ 와 데이트를 하다
- **leave(make) a good impression**: 좋은 인상을 남기다

sentences.text: Do you have any baggage to check?
Yes, I have two suitcases.
sentences.ko: 네, 여행용 가방이 두 개 있어요.

sentences.text: How many bags will you check?
How many bags can I check in?
sentences.ko: 짐을 몇 개까지 부칠 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Please put your baggage on the scale.
Please place your bag on the scale.
Do you have any other baggage?
This is a carry-on bag.
Can I carry this on board?
sentences.ko: 이걸 기내에 가지고 탈 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Can I take this on the plane?
sentences.ko: 이걸 비행기에 가지고 탈 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Your baggage is 1 kg overweight.
You have to pay an extra charge.
How much is the extra charge?
What's the weight limit?
What's the baggage allowance?
I’m calling to make a reservation at seven.
sentences.note:
- **I’m calling to** V: ~ 하려고 전화 했어요
- **make a reservation**: 예약하다

sentences.text: How many in your party, sir?
sentences.note: - **How many in your party?**: (인원이) 몇 명이시죠?

sentences.text: Do you have a room for six?
sentences.note: - **Do you have a room/table for** 숫자?: ~ 인용 방/테이블 있나요?

sentences.text: It makes no difference whether you book or not.
sentences.ko: 예약을 하시든 안 하시든 별 차이가 없어요.
sentences.note: - **make no difference**: 차이가 없다

sentences.text: What do you mean?
sentences.note: - **What do you mean?**: 무슨 뜻이죠?(상대방이 한 말이 이해가 되지 않아서 무슨 의도인지 확인하려고 묻는 표현)

sentences.text: You’ll be admitted on a first-come first-served basis.
sentences.note:
- **be admitted** (to 장소): (~ 에) 입장하다
- **on a** Adj **basis**: ~ 을 기준으로

sentences.text: How can I get to the Express Bus Terminal?
sentences.note: - **How can I get to** 장소?: ~ 까지 어떻게 가나요?

sentences.text: You can take the bus No. 3 across the street.
sentences.note:
- **take the bus/line number**: ~ 번 버스/지하철을 타다
- **across the street**: 길 건너편에서

sentences.text: You mean I have to cross the road?
sentences.note: - **You mean I have to** V: ~ 해야 한다는 뜻이죠?

sentences.text: Right. From what I know, it runs every 20 minutes.
sentences.ko: 네. 제가 알기로는, 매 20분마다 운행을 해요.
sentences.note:
- **From what I know**: 내가 알기로는
- V **every ~ minutes(hours)**: 매 ~ 마다 ~ 를 하다

sentences.text: Thank you. There comes the bus.
sentences.note: - **There(Here) comes** sth: ~ 가 오다

sentences.text: The traffic light is green. Run!
Do you have any metal in your pockets?
No, I have nothing in my pockets.
Please empty your pockets.
Please take out all your belongings.
Please walk through the metal detector.
Please walk through the body scanner.
Please walk through again.
Please take off your shoes and belt.
Remove all liquids from your bag.
Please spread your arms.
Step back, please.
Can you come with me, please?
May I search your bag?
You can't take this on the plane.
sentences.ko: 이것은 기내에 가지고 탈 수 없습니다.

sentences.text: You have to throw it away.
Can you give me a hand with this?
sentences.note: - **give** sb **a hand with** sth: ~ 가 ~ 하는 걸 돕다

sentences.text: I’d love to, but I’m too busy.
How come you’re good at making excuses?
sentences.ko: 넌 왜 그렇게 핑계를 잘 대는거야?
sentences.note:
- **How come** S V?: 왜 ~ 하는 거야?
- **be good at** V-ing(N): ~ 을 잘하다
- **make an excuse**: 핑계를 대다

sentences.text: Don’t take it out on me.
sentences.note: - **take it out on** sb: ~ 에게 화풀이하다

sentences.text: All you have to do is just say yes.
sentences.note: - **All you have to do is** V: ~ 하기만 하면 된다

sentences.text: You have to do it yourself to improve your ability.
sentences.ko: 네 능력을 키우려면, 스스로 해야 해.
sentences.note:
- **do** sth **oneself**: 스스로 ~ 하다
- **improve** one's **ability**: 능력을 키우다

sentences.text: What a nice view! It’s too good to be true.
sentences.note:

sentences.ko: 그녀가 돌아오고 싶어 하는지 알고 싶어.
sentences.note: - **see if** S V: ~ 인지 확인해 보다

sentences.text: After splitting up, it’s good to go your separate ways.
sentences.ko: 헤어진 후엔 각자 길을 가는 게 좋아.
sentences.note:
- **split up**: (남녀가) 헤어지다
- **go** one's **separate ways**: 각자의 길을 가다

sentences.text: Should I give back the things she got me?
sentences.ko: 걔가 나한테 사 준 물건을 돌려줘야 하나?

sentences.text: Just throw them away. What’s the point of keeping them?
sentences.ko: 그냥 버려. 보관하는 게 무슨 소용 있어?
sentences.note:
- **throw** sth **away**: (쓰레기 등)을 버리다
- **What’s the point of** V-ing: ~ 하는 것이 무슨 소용 있어?

sentences.text: I have no idea how I can get over her.
sentences.ko: 그녀를 어떻게 잊을 수 있을지 전혀 모르겠어.
sentences.note:
- **have no idea**: 전혀 모르겠다
- **get over** sb: ~ 를 잊다(극복하다)

sentences.text: I’ll set you up with a nice girl from my class.
sentences.ko: 우리 반에 있는 멋진 여자를 소개시켜 줄게.
sentences.note: - **set** A **up with** B: A에게 B를 소개시켜 주다

sentences.text: I heard you’ve been to Danang recently.
sentences.note: - **have been to** 장소: ~ 에 다녀왔다(가봤다)

sentences.text: It couldn’t be better. I highly recommend it.
sentences.ko: 더할 나위 없이 좋아. 강력 추천해.
sentences.note:
- (sth) **couldn’t be better**: (~ 은) 더할 나위 없이 좋다 | 매우 좋다
- **I highly recommend** sth: ~ 을 강력 추천하다

sentences.text: You got the plane ticket from a low-cost carrier?
sentences.note: - **low-cost carrier**: 저가 항공사

sentences.text: Yeah. It’s easy on the wallet. It only cost around $300.
sentences.note: - **be easy on the wallet**: (가격이) 저렴하다 | 부담이 적다

sentences.text: I’m thrilled to hear it. How about the local cuisine?
sentences.ko: 듣기만 해도 너무 좋아. 현지 음식은 어땠어?
sentences.note:
- **be thrilled to** V: ~ 해도 너무 좋아(신나)
- **local cuisine**: 현지 음식

sentences.text: Mostly the food was not to my taste.
sentences.note: - **be** (not) **to** one’s **taste**: ~의 취향이다(이 아니다) | 입맛에 (안) 맞다

sentences.text: Can you go any faster?
sentences.ko: 좀 더 빨리 가 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: I'd like to, but traffic is backed up.
How long will it take?
Could you slow down, please?
There's no need to hurry.
Please step on it. I'm in a hurry.
I think you're going around.
There's a lot of traffic.
Traffic isn't moving at all.
Please turn right at the next corner.
Please turn left at the next intersection.
Please stop over there for a minute.
Go to the second light, please.
Here we are.
Just keep going.
Are you sure this is what you want to do?
Don’t you get it? I have made that clear.
sentences.ko: 이해 안 돼요? 난 분명히 했어요.
sentences.note: - **make** sth **clear**: ~ 을 분명히 하다

sentences.text: I hate to say this, but you’re dead wrong.
sentences.ko: 이런 말하기 싫지만, 당신이 완전히 틀렸어요.
sentences.note:
- **I hate to say this, but**: 이런 말하기 싫지만
- **dead wrong**: 완전히 틀린

sentences.text: If you don’t trust me, count me out.
sentences.ko: 날 믿지 못할 거라면, 날 빼 주세요.
sentences.note: - **count** sb/sth **out**: ~ 를 제외시키다

sentences.text: Oh, no. Here we go again.
sentences.note: - **Here we go again**: (불평) 또 시작이야 | 정말 못 말리겠군(상대방에게 불쾌감을 주는 상황이나 같은 행동이 반복될 때 사용하는 표현)

sentences.text: What I want you to do is take some action.
sentences.ko: 당신에게 원하는 것은 뭐든 조치를 취하는 거예요.
sentences.note:
- **what I want you to do**: 당신에게 원하는 것
- **take action**: 조치를 취하다

sentences.text: It hits the spot. It’s relieving my hangover.
sentences.note:
- sth **hits the spot**: 바로 이거야(딱 좋아)
- **relieve** one's **hangover**: 숙취가 풀리다

sentences.text: You look terrible. Why did you drink so much?
sentences.ko: 상태가 안좋게 보이네. 왜 그렇게 많이 마셨어?
sentences.note: - **look** Adj: ~ 하게 보이다

sentences.text: No matter how much I drink, it never gets old.
sentences.note:
- **No matter how** + Adj(Adv) S V: 아무리 ~ 하더라도
- **it never gets old**: 질리지 않다

sentences.text: I’m worried that you could get addicted to alcohol.
sentences.note:
- **I’m worried that** S V: ~ 할까 걱정되다
- **get addicted to** sth: ~ 에 중독되다

sentences.text: Thanks for your concern. Let’s go grab some coffee.
sentences.note: - **go grab some coffee**: 커피 마시러 가다

sentences.text: Let’s go to the place at the shopping mall.
Can you stop over there?
I'll drop you off near the subway station.
Would you pull over here?
Please stop at the next light.
Please stop in front of that building.
Can you let me out here?
Please let me out at the next light.
Please drop me off at that corner.
Please drop me off past the intersection.
How much is it?
Do you have change for a hundred?
I don't have any small change.
Here you are.
Keep the change.
Can you take out my baggage?
I owe you an apology. I forgot your birthday.
sentences.ko: 사과할 게 있어. 네 생일을 깜빡했어.
sentences.note: - **owe** sb **an apology**: ~ 에게 사과할 게 있다

sentences.text: Come on. Let it go.
sentences.ko: 뭐 그런 걸 다. 신경 쓰지마.
sentences.note: - **Let it go**: (지난 일은) 신경 쓰지마(그냥 둬)

sentences.text: I promise it’ll never happen again.
sentences.note: - **It’ll never happen again**: 다신 이런 일 없을거야

sentences.text: No problem. It could happen to anyone.
sentences.note: - **happen to** sb: (어떤 일이) ~ 에게 일어나다

sentences.text: I want to make up for missing it.
sentences.ko: 네 기념일을 놓친 걸 보상하고 싶어.
sentences.note: - **make up for** sth: ~ 을 보상하다 | 만회하다

sentences.text: Forget it. I don’t want to twist your arm.
sentences.note:
- **Forget it**: 됐어(신경 쓰지 마)
- **twist** one’s **arm**: 억지로 강요하다 | 엎드려 절 받다

sentences.text: My wife quit her job to be a stay-at-home mom.
sentences.note: - **stay-at-home mom**: 전업주부

sentences.text: She has been struggling with looking after her kids.
sentences.note:
- **struggle with** V-ing(N): ~ 로 힘들어하다
- **looking after** sb/sth: ~ 를 돌보다

sentences.text: I may have to take a part-time job for tuition.
sentences.ko: 교육비 때문에 아르바이트를 해야 할지 모르겠어.
sentences.note: - **take a part-time job**: 아르바이트를 하다

sentences.text: That’s why double-income families are common nowadays.
sentences.ko: 그래서 요즘 맞벌이 가정이 보편화된 거야.
sentences.note: - **double-income family**: 맞벌이 가정

sentences.text: Thanks for listening. It feels good to get that off my chest.
sentences.ko: 들어줘서 고마워. 터놓고 얘기하니 기분 좋다.
sentences.note: - **get** sth **off** one’s **chest**: (고민을) 터놓고 얘기하다

sentences.text: Shooting the breeze is the only way we can relieve stress.
sentences.ko: 수다 떠는 게 유일한 스트레스 해소법이지.
sentences.note:
- **shoot the breeze**: 수다 떨다(잡담하다)
- **relieve stress**: 스트레스를 해소하다

sentences.text: How many stops to Central Station?
It's five stops away from here.
Is there a subway station near here?
Where is the nearest subway station?
Where can I buy a ticket?
Where is the ticket machine?
May I have a subway map?
Which line goes downtown?
Which line goes to South Ferry?
sentences.ko: 사우스 페리로 가는 것은 몇 호선인가요?

sentences.text: Where do I take the train for City Hall?
How much is it to City Hall?
One ticket to City Hall, please.
Can I get a one-day pass?
Can I have a seven-day pass?
Where can I take line number 7?
Why are you in a hurry? Just slow down.
sentences.ko: 왜 이렇게 서둘러요? 좀 천천히 해요.
sentences.note:
- **be in a hurry**: 서두르다(바쁘다)
- **slow down**: 속도를 늦추다

sentences.text: I can’t wait to get married and live with you.
sentences.note: - **can’t wait to** V: ~ 하고 싶어 죽겠다

sentences.text: Just because we go out doesn’t mean we have to get married.
sentences.ko: (남녀가) 사귄다고 해서 결혼해야 하는 건 아니잖아요.
sentences.note:
- **Just because** A **doesn’t mean** B: A 하다고 해서 B 하는 것은 아니다
- **go out**: (남녀가) 사귀다

sentences.text: I see what you mean. Take whatever time you need.
sentences.ko: 무슨 말인지 알아요. 시간을 충분히 가져요.
sentences.note: - **take whatever ~ you need(want)**: 편한 대로 하세요

sentences.text: Now you’re talking.
sentences.note: - **Now you’re talking**: 바로 그거야(서로 다른 얘기를 하다가 어느 순간 대화의 물꼬가 트일 때 쓰는 표현)

sentences.text: People say that we’re a good match.
sentences.note: - **good match**: 좋은 상대, 배우자

sentences.text: Did you see the price of these fruits?
It’s expensive. I think they’re out of season.
sentences.note: - sth **is out of season**: 제철이 아니다(비수기이다)

sentences.text: We can get them for the best price near our place.
sentences.ko: 집 근처에서 저렴하게 구입할 수 있어.
sentences.note: - **get** sth **for the best price**: ~ 을 저렴하게 구입하다

sentences.text: What do we do with the leftovers at home?
sentences.note:
- **leftovers**: 남은 음식
- **What do we do with** sth?: ~ 는 어떻게 하지?

sentences.text: We can put them in the blender to make juice.
Let’s get some dumplings. I’ll be in the frozen food aisle.
sentences.ko: 만두 좀 사자. 냉동식품 코너에 있을게.
sentences.note:
- **be in the ~ aisle**: ~ 코너에 있다
- **frozen food**: 냉동식품

sentences.text: Which line should I transfer to?
You can transfer to line number 3.
Where should I change trains?
Where do I have to transfer?
You should transfer trains at City Hall.
You can transfer to the green line.
I got on the wrong train.
You should take the train on the other side.
Which stop should I get off at?
How many stops until Union Station?
I think I missed my station.
I got on the wrong side of the tracks.
Where is the exit for National Gallery?
Take the exit number 2.
You’re all dressed up for the interview today.
sentences.note: - **be dressed up**: 차려입다(빼입다)

sentences.text: You know what they say, “Clothes make the man.”
sentences.note: - **clothes make the man**: 옷이 날개다

sentences.text: It looks like you got a new suit.
I haven’t bought a new one in six years.
sentences.note: - **haven’t p.p. in** 기간: ~ 동안 ~ 하지 않았다

sentences.text: That’s where you’ve changed. You used to wear wash-and-wear.
sentences.ko: 그 점이 네가 달라진 거구나. 넌 (물빨래해서 입는) 싸구려 옷만 입었잖아.
sentences.note:
- **That’s where** S V: 그 점이 ~ 해진 거야
- **wash-and-wear**: (물빨래해서 입는) 싸구려 옷

sentences.text: Just drop it! Let’s wait and see how the result comes out.
sentences.ko: 좀 그만 해! 어떻게 면접 결과가 나오는지 두고 보자.
sentences.note:
- **drop it**: 됐어(그만해)
- **wait and see**: 두고 보다(지켜 보다)
- **come out**: (결과가) 나오다

sentences.text: I had my car fixed, but it’s been giving me trouble.
sentences.note:
- **have(get)** sth **fixed**: ~ 을 수리하다(고치다)
- sth **has been giving** sb **trouble**: ~ 이 계속 말썽이다

sentences.text: I know the feeling. I’ve been there before.
sentences.ko: 그 기분 알아. 나도 그런 적 있어.
sentences.note:
- **I know the feeling**: 그 기분 알아
- **I’ve been there before**: 나도 그런 적 있어

sentences.text: The mechanic can’t sort things out.
sentences.note: - **sort out** sth: ~ 을 해결(정리)하다

sentences.text: Everytime I visit, he keeps saying “Let me double-check.”
sentences.ko: 갈 때마다 그는 “다시 확인해 볼게요”라고 말하지.

sentences.text: I’ve done a lot of thinking. I have to act now.
sentences.ko: 많은 생각을 했어. 이제 행동을 해야겠어.
sentences.note: - **do a lot of thinking**: 많은 생각을 하다

sentences.text: So what? Are you gonna sue the car company?
sentences.note:
- **So what?**: 어쩌려고? | 그래서 어쩔 건데?
- **sue** sb: ~ 을 고소하다

sentences.text: Is this the right train for Seattle?
Yes, you can take this train.
A ticket to Boston, please.
I'd like a round-trip ticket, please.
Which train goes to Chicago?
When is the earliest train to Denver?
sentences.ko: 덴버로 가는 가장 빠른 기차가 언제인가요?

sentences.text: When is the next train for New York?
What time does the train leave?
How often does the train run?
What's the fare to Sydney?
Where can I take the train for London?
Is this the right platform for Manchester?
Is this going to Edinburgh?
Is this train bound for Oxford?
Is this the train for Brighton?

lessons.title: 단것 좀 그만 먹어 | 렌터카 문의

sentences.text: Honey, what do you think of these sunglasses?
sentences.note: - **What do you think of** sb/sth?: ~ 를 어떻게 생각해?

sentences.text: You’re going on a vacation or something?
sentences.note: - **go on a vacation**: 휴가를 떠나다

sentences.text: Give me a break. I was just trying them out.
sentences.note:
- **Give me a break**: 한번만 봐줘
- **try** sth **out**: (시험 삼아) 착용하다

sentences.text: I’m gonna take our kids to the ice cream stand.
sentences.note: - **take** sb **to** 장소: ~ 를 ~ 에 데리고 가다

sentences.text: OK. Let’s meet in the food court when I’m done.
Suit yourself. Don’t buy anything on impulse.
sentences.note:
- **Suit yourself**: (상대방이 의사를 물을 때) 마음대로 해
- **buy** sth **on impulse**: 충동구매하다

sentences.text: I have a craving for something sweet.
sentences.note: - **have a craving for** sth: ~가 당기다(먹고 싶다)

sentences.text: You have a sweet tooth. You want some candy?
sentences.note: - **have a sweet tooth**: 단 것을 좋아하다

sentences.text: No. I’ll have a cheese burger for a snack.
That won't be easy on your stomach.
sentences.note: - **be easy on** one’s **stomach**: 위에 부담이 없다

sentences.text: Sometimes I love getting a taste of junk food.
sentences.ko: 가끔은 인스턴트 식품 먹는 게 좋아.
sentences.note:
- **get a taste of(for)** sth: ~ 을 맛보다 | ~ 의 맛을 알다
- **junk food**: 인스턴트 식품

sentences.text: I see. You can microwave it over there.
What kind of car do you want?
A compact car, please.
I'd like to rent a car.
I'd like to rent a car for three days.
How long will you use it?
For two days.
What kind of cars do you have?
What type of car would you like?
I'd like a compact car.
A midsize car, please.
I want an automatic SUV.
Do you have any convertibles?
I'd like something bigger.
Fill out this form, please.
Can I see your driver's license?
I can’t remember a thing about last night.
sentences.note: - **can’t remember a thing**: 아무 기억이 안 나다

sentences.text: Me, neither. I’m in the mood for a beer tonight.
sentences.ko: 나도 그래. 저녁에 맥주 한잔 하고 싶다.
sentences.note: - **be in the mood for** sth: ~ 을 하고 싶은 기분이다

sentences.text: Again? I’m suffering from a terrible hangover.
sentences.note: - **suffer from** sth: ~ 으로 고통받다

sentences.text: Let’s go get hangover soup before hitting the bars.
sentences.ko: 술 마시러 가기 전에 해장국 좀 먹자.
sentences.note:
- **hangover soup**: 해장국(hangover chaser)
- **hit the bars**: 술 마시러 가다

sentences.text: Perfect. Let’s get wasted tonight.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 오늘 밤에 진탕 마셔 보자.
sentences.note: - **get wasted**: 만취하다

sentences.text: I’ll get the bill this time.
sentences.note: - **get the bill**: (음식 값을) 지불하다

sentences.text: Look how cute it is! Can I pet it?
sentences.note:
- **Look how** Adj(Adv) S V!: 엄청 ~ 하구나!
- **pet** sth/sb: ~ 을 살짝 만져보다

sentences.text: Of course. I adopted it about a month ago.
sentences.note: - **adopt** sth/sb: ~ 을 입양하다

sentences.text: Dogs are high-maintenance pets.
sentences.note: - sth **is high-maintenance**: 손이 많이 가다

sentences.text: Yes, but it’s okay because I’m a dog person.
sentences.ko: 맞아, 하지만 난 개를 좋아하는 사람이니까 괜찮아.
sentences.note: - **dog person**: 개를 좋아하는 사람

sentences.text: I’m allergic to animal fur. So I can’t keep them.
sentences.ko: 난 동물 털에 알레르기가 있어. 그래서 못 키워.
sentences.note:
- **be allergic to** sth: ~ 에 알레르기가 있다
- **keep animals**: 동물을 기르다

sentences.text: Just make yourself at home. I’ll get some drinks.
sentences.ko: 편하게 있어. 마실 것 좀 가져올게.
sentences.note: - **make yourself at home**: 편하게 있어

sentences.text: Do you want insurance?
I'd like full coverage, please.
What's the daily rate?
What's the rental fee?
I'd like to get insurance.
I'll take the minimum insurance coverage.
How much is insurance?
Does it include insurance?
Do you offer GPS navigation?
Do you have a car seat?
I'd like to see the car before I rent it.
sentences.ko: 렌트하기 전에 차를 먼저 보고 싶어요.

sentences.text: I'll take this car.
How much do you charge if I'm late?
I'm here to return the car.
Our kids always fight over nothing.
sentences.ko: 우리 애들은 맨날 사소한 일로 싸워.
sentences.note: - **fight over nothing**: 사소한 일로 싸우다

sentences.text: It’s no big deal. Never mind.
sentences.note:
- **It’s no big deal**: 별일(대단한 일) 아니야
- **Never mind**: 신경 쓰지 마

sentences.text: I agree with you to some degree, but I’m a little sensitive.
sentences.ko: 어느 정도까지 너에게 동의하는데, 내가 좀 예민한가 봐.
sentences.note:
- **agree with** sb: ~ 에게 동의하다
- **to some degree**: 어느 정도까지

sentences.text: They have no trouble adjusting to school life?
sentences.ko: 학교 생활에 적응하는 데는 문제 없어?
sentences.note:
- **have trouble** V-ing: ~ 하는 데 어려움을 겪다
- **adjust to** V-ing(N): ~ 에 적응하다

sentences.text: Yes, I guess so.
I bet they’ll grow up to be great people.
sentences.ko: 우리 애들은 커서 훌륭한 사람이 될 거야.
sentences.note: - **grow up to be** N: 커서 ~ 가 되다

sentences.text: Somebody put the fake story online.
sentences.note: - **put** sth **online**: 인터넷에 올리다

sentences.text: I saw that on Youtube. It went viral.
sentences.note: - sth **goes viral**: 쫙 퍼지다(입소문 나다)

sentences.text: Why do they make stuff up like that?
sentences.note: - **make** sth **up**: ~ 을 꾸며내다

sentences.text: They want to draw attention and people fall for it easily.
sentences.ko: 관심을 끌고 싶고, 사람들이 잘 속으니까.
sentences.note:
- **draw** (one’s) **attention** (to): (~ 의) 관심을 (~로) 끌다
- **fall for** sth: ~ 에 속다

sentences.text: The thing is some people go over the line.
sentences.ko: 문제는 일부 사람들이 도를 넘어서는 것이야.
sentences.note:
- **The thing is** S V: 문제는 ~ 이다
- **go(be) over the line**: 도를 넘어서다

sentences.text: That’s why we need to have good judgment.
sentences.note: - **have good judgment**: 판단력이 좋다 | 식견이 있다

Let's stop at the gas station.
We are running out of gas.
Is there a gas station nearby?

Fill it up, please.
$20, please.
Fill her up to $50.
Unleaded, please.
Can you move up a little, please?
Turn off the engine, please.
How can I use this gas pump?
Can you show me how to use this pump?
sentences.ko: 이 주유기 어떻게 쓰는지 알려 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Where is the next gas station?

sentences.note: - **way too** Adj: 너무 ~ 하다

sentences.text: You’re not wearing that to the party.
sentences.ko: 너 그 옷을 입고 파티에 가지 못해.
sentences.note: - **wear** sth **to the party**: ~ 을 입고 파티에 가다

sentences.text: Mom! You don’t have an eye for fashion.
sentences.note: - **have an eye for** sth: ~ 에 대한 안목이 있다

sentences.text: You’re impossible. You look good in everything.
sentences.ko: 넌 구제불능이야. 넌 아무거나 입어도 잘 어울려.
sentences.note:
- **You’re impossible**: 넌 구제불능이야
- A **look good in** B: A에게 B가 잘 어울린다

sentences.text: Please stop! You never take my side at all.
sentences.ko: 그만해요! 내 편은 전혀 안 들어 주잖아요.
sentences.note: - **take** one’s **side**: ~ 의 편을 들다

sentences.text: It’s terribly hot. This is murder.
sentences.note: - **This is murder**: 살인적이야

sentences.text: It’s still May, but it’s already hot.
But I prefer a hot summer to a cold winter.
sentences.ko: 그래도 추운 겨울보다 더운 여름이 더 좋아.
sentences.note: - **prefer** A **to** B: B보다 A가 더 좋다

sentences.text: That reminds me, you don’t seem to sweat a lot.
sentences.ko: 그러고 보니, 넌 땀을 많이 흘리지는 않는 것 같은데.
sentences.note:
- **That reminds me**: 그러고 보니
- **don’t seem to** V: ~ 하지 않는 것 같다
- **sweat a lot**: 땀을 많이 흘리다

sentences.text: Since you bring it up, let’s get some exercise.
sentences.ko: 말 나온 김에, 운동이나 좀 하자.
sentences.note:
- **Since you bring it up**: 말 나온 김에
- **get some exercise**: 운동을 좀 하다

sentences.text: I’ll buy an iced coffee after working up a sweat.
sentences.ko: 땀 흘리고 나서 냉커피 한잔 살게.
sentences.note: - **work up a sweat**: 땀을 흘리다

Let's see. You need an oil change.
My car broke down.
I can't start the engine.
I have a flat tire.
Would you check my tires?

The AC is not working.
The brake doesn't work properly.
My car is making a funny noise.
There is something wrong with my car.
I'm afraid the battery is dead.
The GPS navigation system stopped working.
How can I change language setting to Korean?
I had to stay up all night cramming for the finals.
sentences.note:
- **stay up all night**: 밤새다(날새기하다)(새벽까지 공부하거나 아픈 사람을 간호하면서 뜬눈으로 지샐 때 사용하는 표현)
- **cramm**: 벼락치기를 하다

sentences.text: Now it’s party time. Live it up.
sentences.ko: 이제 파티 할 때야. 맘껏 즐기자고.
sentences.note: - **live it up**: 신나게 즐기다 | (돈을 펑펑 쓰며) 살다

sentences.text: Is it OK if I invite someone to the party?
As long as it’s not Henry. He’s such a party pooper.
sentences.ko: 헨리만 아니면 돼. 분위기 망치는 녀석이야.
sentences.note: - **party pooper**: 분위기 망치는 사람

sentences.text: OK. We might as well keep it a secret from him.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 그럼 비밀로 하는 게 낫겠다.
sentences.note: - **keep it a secret**: 비밀로 하다

sentences.text: Come on! Let’s get a move on!
sentences.note: - **get a move on**: 서두르다

sentences.text: You know what? Can I ask you a favor?
sentences.note:
- **You know what?**: 있잖아
- **ask** sb **a favor**: ~ 에게 좀 부탁하다

sentences.text: Sure. Go ahead. What is it?
sentences.note: - **Go ahead**: 어서 말해 봐

sentences.text: I’m going to take a short trip. Can you watch my dog?
sentences.note:
- **take a** (short) **trip**: (단기) 여행을 가다
- **watch** sth: ~ 을 봐주다

sentences.text: No problem. You know I’m a dog person.
sentences.note: - **dog person**: 개를 좋아하는 사람

sentences.text: Thanks for your help. I’ll get you a present.
sentences.note: - **get** sb **a present**: ~ 에게 선물을 사주다

sentences.text: All right if you insist. Have a safe trip!
sentences.ko: 정 그렇다면 좋아. 여행 잘 다녀와!
sentences.note:
- **All right if you insist**: 정 그렇다면 좋아.
- **Have a safe trip!**: 여행 잘 다녀와!

sentences.text: How did it happen?
I got rear-ended.
Hello, is this the police station?

Someone ran into my car.
I just had a fender-bender.
I got rear-ended by another car.
It was a head-on collision.
My car was hit head-on.
That car hit mine broadside.
sentences.ko: 저 차가 제 차 옆면을 들이받았어요.

sentences.text: I was in a five-car pileup.
Why did you hurt her feelings?
sentences.note: - **hurt** one's **feelings**: ~ 의 감정을 상하게 하다

sentences.text: I didn’t mean to.
sentences.note: - **didn’t mean to** V: 일부러 ~ 한 건 아니다

sentences.text: Watch your language and don’t swear ever again.
sentences.note:
- **Watch your language**: (상대방이 말을 함부로 할 때) 말조심해
- **swear**: 욕을 하다

sentences.text: I’m sorry. I’ll keep that in mind.
sentences.note: - **keep** sth **in mind**: 명심하다(기억해 두다)

sentences.text: How many times do I have to tell you the same things?
sentences.ko: 대체 몇 번을 같은 얘기를 말해야겠어?
sentences.note: - **How many times do I have to** V: 대체 몇 번을 ~ 해야 하니?

sentences.text: I don’t know what to say.
sentences.note: - **don’t know what to say**: 뭐라고 할 말이 없다

sentences.text: I’m so beat. I haven’t hit the gym in ages.
sentences.ko: 너무 지쳤어. 정말 오랫동안 (운동하러) 헬스장에 가지않았어.
sentences.note:
- **beat**: 지친(피곤한)
- **hit the gym**: (운동하러) 헬스장에 가다

sentences.text: Any special reason for working out that hard?
sentences.ko: 운동을 열심히 하는 특별한 이유가 있니?

sentences.text: I pigged out during the holiday. I have to pay for it.
sentences.note:
- **pig out** (on sth): ~ 을 과식하다(실컷 먹다)
- **pay for** sth: 대가를 지불하다

sentences.text: You’re looking good for now. Don’t overdo it.
sentences.ko: 지금도 좋아 보이는데. 너무 무리하지 마.
sentences.note:
- **look good** (for now): (지금도) 좋아 보인다
- **overdo**: 무리하다

sentences.ko: 나를 기분 좋게 해주려고 하는 말인 거 알아.
sentences.note: - **make** sb **feel better**: ~ 를 기분 좋게 해주다

sentences.text: No, I’m serious. I don’t know how to lie.

That car stopped suddenly.
That car came out of nowhere.
This car hit me from behind.
sentences.ko: 이 차가 제 차를 뒤에서 들이받았어요.

I sprained my neck.

I was hit by a car.

My friend was hit by a car.

sentences.note: - **be attracted to** sb: ~ 에게 매력을 느끼다

sentences.ko: 좀 창피하긴 한데, 그녀에게 푹 빠졌어.
sentences.note: - **be into** sb/sth: ~ 에 빠지다(좋아하다)

sentences.ko: 꿈도 꾸지 마. 너에게 과분한 여자야.

- **Don’t even think about it**: 꿈도 꾸지마(실현 가능성이 전혀 없는데 기대부터 잔뜩 하는 사람에게 쓰는 표현)
- **out of one's league**: ~ 에게 과분한

sentences.text: Is she seeing someone?

sentences.note: - **already taken**: 이미 임자가 있는

sentences.text: I’m just gonna ask her out. It won’t hurt to try.
sentences.ko: 데이트 신청이나 해 봐야지. 손해 볼 건 없잖아.
sentences.note:
- **ask** sb **out**: ~ 에게 데이트 신청하다
- **It won’t hurt to try**: 손해 볼 건 없다 | 밑져야 본전이다

- **late at night**: 밤늦은 시간에

sentences.note:

sentences.note:

sentences.note: - **I’ll have my usual**: 늘 먹던 거 주세요

sentences.note: - **Make it a double, please**: 곱배기로 주세요.

sentences.ko: 제 꺼는 좀 덜 맵게 해 주세요.

sentences.note: - sth **is a killer**: ~ 가 끝내준다

sentences.text: I got stuck in traffic near the City Hall.

sentences.text: Traffic is heavy at this time of day.
sentences.ko: 하루 중 이 시간에 교통이 혼잡해.
sentences.note:
- **traffic is heavy**: 차가 밀리다
- **at this time of day**: 하루 중 이 시간에

sentences.note: - **I’ve been wanting to** V: 예전부터 ~ 하고 싶었다

- **have** sth **in mind**: ~ 을 마음에 두다

- **end up** V-ing: 결국 ~ 하게 되다
- **buy** (sth) **in bulk**: ~ 을 대량으로 구매하다

sentences.text: but we can save time because we don’t have to keep going back.
sentences.ko: 자주 안 가도 되니 시간을 절약하는 거잖아.
sentences.note: - **keep** V-ing: 자주(계속) ~ 하다

sentences.text: You can order online. It’ll save you the trouble.
sentences.ko: 온라인으로 주문해 봐. 수고를 덜어 줄 거야.
sentences.note:
- **order** sth **online**: 온라인으로 주문하다
- **save** sb **the trouble** (of + V-ing): ~ 하는 수고를 덜다

sentences.text: Front desk, how may I help you?
This is room 502. There's no hot water.

I can't open the window.
When was the last time you got a medical checkup?
sentences.ko: 마지막으로 건강 검진 한 게 언제죠?
sentences.note:
- **When was the last time** S V?: 마지막으로 ~ 한 게 언제죠?
- **get a medical checkup**: 건강 검진을 받다

sentences.text: Two months ago. I get it at my company every year.
How did it go this time?
sentences.note: - **How did** sth **go?**: 결과가 어떻게 되었나요?

sentences.text: Not good. My blood pressure went up a bit.
sentences.note: - **go up**: (수치, 혈압이) 올라가다

sentences.text: You’ve been under a lot of stress lately.
sentences.note: - **be under a lot of stress**: 스트레스를 많이 받다

sentences.text: I should take good care of my health.
sentences.note: - **take good care of** sb/sth: ~ 을 각별히 보살피다

sentences.text: I really feel like a beer. What about you?
sentences.ko: 맥주 한잔을 하고 싶어. 넌 어때?
sentences.note:
- **feel like** V-ing: ~ 을 하고(먹고) 싶다
- **What about you?**: 넌 어때?

sentences.text: There’s nothing better than a cold one after work.
sentences.ko: 일 끝나고 시원한 맥주보다 나은 게 없지.
sentences.note:
- **There’s nothing better than** sth: ~ 보다 나은 게 없다
- **cold one**: 시원한 맥주

sentences.text: Let’s shoot some pool after having some beer.
sentences.note: - **shoot(play) some pool**: 포켓볼을 치다

sentences.text: OK. Is there a good place to go around here?
sentences.ko: 좋아. 이 근처에 갈 만한 곳이 있어?
sentences.note: - **Is there a good place to** V: ~ 할 만한 곳이 있어?

sentences.text: I know a place where we can drink out on the patio.
sentences.ko: 야외 테라스에서 마실 수 있는 곳을 알고 있어.
sentences.note: - **out on the patio**: 야외 테라스에서

sentences.text: I love those places. Let’s go.
sentences.ko: 나 그런 데 좋아해. 어서 가자.

sentences.text: The toilet won't flush.
I'll send someone to fix it.
We're out of toilet paper.
The toilet is clogged.
The toilet is overflowing.
The bidet is not working.
The sink is clogged up.
The drain is blocked.
The shower doesn't work.
The room key doesn't work.
I locked myself out.
I'm locked out of my room.
sentences.ko: 방 문이 잠겨서 들어갈 수가 없어요.

sentences.text: I can't find my key anywhere.
sentences.ko: 열쇠를 아무 데서도 찾을 수가 없어요.

sentences.text: The room next door is too noisy.
I'd like to change my room.
Can you help me with my math homework?
sentences.ko: 내가 수학 숙제 하는 것을 도와줄 수 있어?
sentences.note: - **help** sb **with** N: ~ 가 ~ 하는 것을 돕다

sentences.text: Sorry, I can’t. My hands are full.
sentences.ko: 미안하지만 안 되겠어. 지금 좀 바빠.
sentences.note: - One’s **hands are full**: 정신없이 바쁘다

sentences.text: Math tests are not what they used to be.
sentences.note: - **be not what it used to be**: 예전 같지 않다

sentences.text: What can I say? You have to get used to it.
sentences.note:
- **What can I say?**: (체념) 어쩌겠어?
- **get used to** V-ing/N: ~ 에 익숙해지다

sentences.text: Math is not my thing, but English is my favorite.
sentences.ko: 수학은 나하고 안 맞아. 영어는 좋아하는데.
sentences.note: - Sth **is not my thing**: ~ 은 내 취향이 아니다 | ~ 를 싫어하다

sentences.text: If so, you should play to your strengths.
sentences.note: - **play to** one’s **strengths**: 강점을 발휘하다

sentences.text: Is everything okay? Let’s talk over coffee.
sentences.note:
- **Is everything okay?**: 별일 없지?
- **over coffee**: 커피 마시면서

sentences.text: I have no time for rest. I have a report to finish.
sentences.ko: 쉴 시간이 없어. 보고서를 끝내야 해.
sentences.note: - **have no time for** N: (부정적) ~ 할 시간이 없다

sentences.text: I can’t remember the last time we talked.
sentences.ko: 우리가 언제 대화했는지 기억도 안 나.
sentences.note: - **can’t remember the last time** S V: 언제 ~ 했는지 기억도 안 난다

sentences.text: I’m behind in my work. It’ll only take a few hours.
sentences.ko: 일이 좀 밀려 있거든. 몇 시간이면 될 거야.
sentences.note: - sb **is behind in** one’s **work**: 일이 밀려 있다

sentences.text: Well, you deserve recognition for hard work.
sentences.ko: 하여튼, 열심히 하는 것은 인정받을 만해.
sentences.note: - **deserve recognition for** sth: ~ 는 인정받을 만하다

sentences.text: I’m just doing my job. Stop flattering me.
sentences.ko: 그냥 내 일을 하는거야. 나에게 듣기 좋은 말을 하지마.
sentences.note:
- **do** one's **job**: 자기 일을 하다
- **flatter** sb: ~ 에게 듣기 좋은 말을 하다

sentences.text: What time is check-out?
You should check out by 12:00.
Check out, please.
I'd like to check out, please.
When is check-out time?
Can I check out late?
How much is the late check-out?
How much is the charge?
What is this charge for?
sentences.ko: 이 청구 금액은 무엇에 대한 건가요?

sentences.text: I didn't use the mini bar.
I didn't get any room service.
How would you like to pay?
I'd like to pay by credit card.
Could you keep my baggage?
sentences.ko: 제 짐을 맡아 주실 수 있나요?

My stomach feels heavy from indigestion.
sentences.note: - one's **stomach feels heavy**: 속이 더부룩하다

sentences.text: You shouldn’t have eaten so much at the buffet.
sentences.ko: 뷔페에서 너무 많이 먹지 말았어야 했어.
sentences.note: - **shouldn’t have** p.p.: ~ 하지 말았어야 했어

sentences.text: You talked me into going there.
sentences.note: - **talk** sb **into** V-ing: ~ 를 ~ 하도록 설득하다

sentences.text: Don’t blame me for your eating too much.
sentences.ko: 네가 과식한 걸 내 탓으로 돌리지 마.
sentences.note: - **blame** sb **for** sth: ~ 때문에 ~ 를 탓하다

sentences.text: I need to go on a diet or something.
sentences.note: - **go on a diet**: 다이어트하다

sentences.text: I can’t take it anymore. I hate the way you talk.
sentences.ko: 더 이상 못 참겠어. 내 말투가 정말 싫어.
sentences.note:
- **can’t take it anymore**: 더 이상 못 참다(인내력이 다해서 더 이상 참기 힘들 때 사용하는 표현)
- **hate the way** S V: ~ 하는 방식이 마음에 안 들다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 더위 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 자
sentences.text: Hey, how are you holding up?
sentences.note: - **How are you holding up?**: (힘든 상황) 어떻게 지내?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 더위 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 자
sentences.text: Just getting by. The heat keeps me up at night.
sentences.ko: 그럭저럭 지내. 더위 때문에 밤에 잠을 설쳤어.
sentences.note:
- (Just) **getting by**: 그럭저럭 지내
- sth **keeps** sb **up**: ~ 때문에 잠을 설치다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 더위 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 자
sentences.text: I think I’m more tired because I have late nights.
sentences.ko: 나는 밤 늦게 자니까 더 피곤한 것 같아.
sentences.note: - **have a late night**: 밤 늦게 자다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 더위 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 자
sentences.text: I can’t wait until the summer is over.
sentences.note: - **can’t wait until** N(S V): 빨리 ~ 가 왔으면 좋겠다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 더위 때문에 밤에 잠을 못 자
sentences.text: How about going to a valley this weekend?
sentences.note: - **go to a valley**: 계곡으로 가다

sentences.note: - **Sounds perfect!**: 정말 좋아!

I’m freezing to death. You should bundle up when going out.

- **bundle up**: (옷을) 따뜻하게 입다(껴입다)

- **doze off**: 깜빡 졸다
- **behind the wheel**: 운전 중인

- **miss** sth: ~ 을 못보다(놓치다)
- **be in the middle of** sth: ~ 을 하는 중이다

sentences.note:
- **win/lose** sth **by the score of** 점수: ~의 점수로 지다/이기다
- **close**: 아슬아슬한(아까운)

sentences.text: They’re on a six-game losing streak. I guess they’re in a slump.
sentences.note:
- **be on a** 게임 수 **winning/losing streak**: ~ 연승/연패 중이다
- **be in a slump**: 슬럼프에 빠지다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 그들은 슬럼프에 빠진 것 같아
sentences.text: It’s okay. There’s always a trade off.
sentences.note: - **There is** (always) **a trade-off**: (언제나) 양면이 있기 마련이다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 그들은 슬럼프에 빠진 것 같아

sentences.note: - **win/lose the ~ Series**: ~시리즈에서 우승/패배하다

sentences.ko: 인스턴트 라면 찾는 것 좀 도와주시겠어요?

Give me two, please.
Buy two and get one free.

- **Hold on, please**: (사무실에 온 전화를 바꿔 줄 때) 잠시만 기다려 주세요
- **step out**: 잠시 나가다

sentences.text: It’s so hard to reach him. He was out of town last time.
sentences.ko: 통화하기 어렵네요. 지난 번에 출장 가셨던데.
sentences.note: - **be out of town**: 출장 중이다

sentences.text: I’ll tell him to get back to you when he gets in.
sentences.note:
- **get back to** sb: ~ 에게 회신 전화하다
- **gets in**: (사무실에) 들어오다

sentences.text: It’s almost lunch time. Maybe he’s out to lunch.
sentences.ko: 점심시간이 다 됐네요. 점심 먹으러 외출하셨나 봐요.
sentences.note: - **be out to lunch**: 점심 먹으러 외출하다

sentences.text: We’re almost halfway through the year.
sentences.note: - **be halfway through** sth: 절반쯤 지나다(끝내다)

sentences.text: The older we get, the faster time seems to go.
sentences.ko: 나이 들수록 시간이 더 빨리 가는 것 같아.
sentences.note: - **the 비교급** S V, **the 비교급** S V: ~ 할수록 ~ 하다

sentences.text: Right. I feel like I’m getting fatter than before.
sentences.ko: 맞아. 살도 예전보다 더 찌는 것 같아.
sentences.note: - **get + 비교급 + than before**: 예전보다 더 ~ 하다

sentences.text: Your metabolic rate slows down. You have to eat less and move more.
sentences.ko: 신진대사율이 둔화되잖아. 덜 먹고 더 움직여야 해.
sentences.note:
- **metabolic rate**: 신진대사율
- **eat less and move more**: 덜 먹고 더 움직이다

sentences.text: I’ll stop eating fatty food and start exercising.
sentences.ko: 기름진 음식 그만 먹고 운동 시작할거야.
sentences.note: - **fatty food**: 기름진 음식

sentences.text: You should maintain a healthy weight to stay fit.
sentences.ko: 건강을 유지하려면 적정 체중을 유지해야 해.
sentences.note:
- **maintain a healthy weight**: 적정 체중을 유지하다
- **stay fit**: 건강을 유지히다

I'm just looking around.
Can I help you find something?
Are you being helped?

sentences.ko: 요 며칠 비디오 게임에 중독되어 있어서 그래.
sentences.note: - **be hooked on** sth: ~ 에 중독되어 있다

sentences.text: How old are you? You should act your age.
sentences.ko: 너 몇 살이냐? 나잇값 좀 해라.
sentences.note: - **act** one’s **age**: 나이값을 하다 | 철이 들다

sentences.text: Look who’s talking. Mind your own business.
sentences.ko: 사돈 남 말 하시네. 너나 잘해.
sentences.note:
- **Look who’s talking**: 사돈 남 말 하네
- **Mind your own business**: 너나 잘 해

sentences.text: Don’t lecture me. I’ll kick your ass.
sentences.ko: 잔소리 좀 그만해. 너를 혼날 줄거야.
sentences.note:
- **lecture**: 잔소리(설교)하다
- **kick** one's **ass**: ~ 를 혼내 주다

sentences.text: OK. Let’s just come to our senses.
sentences.note: - **come to** one’s **senses**: 제 정신이 들다

sentences.text: I think my eyesight got worse recently.
sentences.note:
- **eyesight**: 시력(vision)
- **get worse**: ~이 나빠지다(약화되다)

sentences.text: It comes with old age. My vision is blurry at night.
sentences.ko: 노안이 온 거야. 나도 저녁에 눈이 흐릿해.
sentences.note: - **blurry**: 흐릿한

sentences.text: My goodness! That’s what I’ve been afraid of.

sentences.note: - **get** sth **checked**: ~ 을 검사 받다

sentences.text: It’s been on my mind, but I haven’t gotten around to it.
sentences.note:
- sth **is(have sth) on** one’s **mind**: ~ 가 마음에 걸리다
- **get around to** sth: (마침내) ~ 할 시간을 내다

sentences.text: You got your hands full taking care of your kids.
sentences.note:
- **have(get)** one’s **hands full** V-ing: ~ 하느라 너무 바쁘다
- **take care of** sb: ~ 를 돌보다

I wear a large.

Can you measure me?

The fitting room is over there.

This jacket is in fashion now.
It looks great on you.
Which looks better?
I'd prefer a black one.

lessons.title: 고기가 안 잡혀 | 다른 물건 요청

sentences.text: Since when did you get interested in the latest gadgets?

sentences.text: I keep up with trends. I wasn’t born yesterday.

- **rub it in**: 아픈 데를 건드리다 | 염장 지르다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 뭐든 다 먹을 수 있을 것 같아
sentences.text: I got a lot of bites, but mostly came up empty-handed.
sentences.note: - **come** (up) **empty-handed**: 허탕치다(빈손으로 오다)

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 뭐든 다 먹을 수 있을 것 같아
sentences.text: Let’s get ready to cook. I’m so hungry I could eat a horse.
sentences.ko: 요리할 준비를 하자. 배고파 죽을 것 같아.
sentences.note:
- **get ready to** V: ~ 할 준비를 하다
- **I could eat a horse**: 배고파 죽을 것 같다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 뭐든 다 먹을 수 있을 것 같아
sentences.text: I feel thirsty. Where did you put the beers?
sentences.note: - **feel thirsty**: 목이 마르다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 뭐든 다 먹을 수 있을 것 같아
sentences.text: They’re in the blue cooler next to the rock.
sentences.ko: 바위 옆에 청색 아이스박스 안에 있어.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 뭐든 다 먹을 수 있을 것 같아
sentences.text: We should set up the tent before it gets dark.
sentences.note:
- **set up the tent**: 텐트를 치다
- **get dark**: 어두워지다

sentences.text: Do you have this in blue?
Sorry, we don't have it in that color.
Do you have a bigger one?
Do you have a smaller one?
Do you have this in a smaller size?
Do you have this in a larger size?
Do you have this in another size?
Do you have this in a size six?
We don't have that in your size.
Do you have this in another color?
Can you show me another color?
Do you have a red one?
Do you have any other style?
Do you have any other designs?
We're out of that item.
You’ll never guess what happened last night.
sentences.ko: 어젯밤 무슨 일이 있었는지 상상도 못할걸.
sentences.note: - **You’ll never guess wh-** S V: ~ 했는지 상상도 못할걸

sentences.text: What? She stood you up or what?
sentences.note: - **stand** sb **up**: ~ 를 바람맞히다

sentences.text: Exactly. Don’t you think she plays hard to get?
sentences.ko: 맞아. 걔 너무 튕기는 거 아냐?
sentences.note: - **play hard to get**: 튕기다(까다롭게 굴다)

sentences.text: I’m sure she really likes to play the field.
sentences.ko: 확실히 걔는 여러 사람과 사귀는 걸 좋아해.
sentences.note: - **play the field**: 여러 사람과 사귀다

sentences.text: According to rumors, she has feelings for you.
sentences.ko: 소문에 걔가 너한테 마음이 있다고 하던데.
sentences.note: - **have feelings for** sb: ~ 에게 마음이 있다

sentences.text: I don’t buy it. I have a lot on my mind.
sentences.note:
- **don’t buy it**: 믿을 수 없다(눈앞의 상황을 보거나 듣고도 믿지 못할 때 사용하는 표현)
- **have a lot on** one’s **mind**: 생각이 많다 | 머리가 복잡하다

sentences.text: Holy cow! What's up with all the noise?
sentences.note: - **What's up with** sb/sth: ~ 는 대체 뭐야?

sentences.text: It’s the upstairs neighbors. I’ll bring it up with them.
sentences.note: - **bring it up with** sb: ~ 에게 (불편한) 말을 꺼내다

sentences.text: It’s dead serious. How do you put up with it?
sentences.note: - **put up with** sth: ~ 을 참다(견디다)

sentences.text: Besides the noise, they’re really good people.
sentences.note: - **besides** sth: ~ 를 제외하면

sentences.text: Are you standing up for them? You’re really something.
sentences.note:
- **stand up for** sb/sth: ~을 지지(옹호)하다
- **be really something**: 정말 대단하다

sentences.text: I can see where you’re coming from. That’s how you live in an apartment building.
sentences.ko: 무슨 말인지 알아. 아파트에 사는것은 그런거야.
sentences.note:
- **I can see where you’re coming from**: 무슨 말인지 알아
- **That’s how** S V: ~ 는 그런거야

sentences.text: How do you like it?
It's too loose for me.
It fits me well.
It doesn't fit me.
It's too small for me.
It's tight around my chest.
This doesn't work. It's too small.
It's too tight under the arms.
The sleeves are too short.
The sleeves are too long.
This is too tight for me.
I want more room around the shoulders.
sentences.ko: 어깨 쪽 품이 좀 더 넉넉했으면 좋겠어요.

sentences.text: They aren't long enough.
They're tight in the hips.
They're a little loose around the waist.
How old do I look?
sentences.note: - **How** (old) **do I look?**: (나이가) 어때 보여요?

sentences.text: Well, I thought you’re in your mid-30s.
sentences.note: - **be in** one's **mid-30s**: 30대 중반이다

sentences.text: Actually, I’m pushing 40.
sentences.note: - **be pushing 40**: 곧 40세가 되다

sentences.text: Really? You look young for your age.
sentences.note: - **look young for** one’s **age**: 나이에 비해 젊어 보인다

sentences.text: Thanks. I get that a lot. What are you up for?
sentences.ko: 고마워요. 그런 말 많이 들어요. 무엇을 먹고 싶으세요?
sentences.note:
- **get that a lot**: 그런 말 많이 듣는다
- **be up for** sth: ~ 을 먹고(마시고) 싶다

sentences.text: Anything. I’m not picky about food.
sentences.ko: 뭐든지 좋아요. 음식에 대해 까다롭지 않아요.
sentences.note: - **be picky about** sth: ~ 에 대해 까다롭다

sentences.text: How is it going with your boyfriend?
sentences.note: - **How is it going with** sb/sth: ~ 는 어떻게 되고 있어?

sentences.text: We broke up last week after a big fight.
sentences.note: - **break up**: 헤어지다

sentences.text: Not again! You guys will make up in the end.
sentences.note:
- **Not again!**: 또야?
- **make up**: 화해하다

sentences.text: We’re history. I hate already moved on.
sentences.note:
- **We’re history**: 우린 끝났어
- **move on** (to sth): 새로 시작하다 | ~ 로 넘어가다

sentences.text: Don’t worry. There’s a lid for every pot.
sentences.note: - **There’s a lid for every pot**: 짚신도 짝이 있다

sentences.text: I’ve had enough of him bossing me around.
sentences.ko: 그가 나에게 이래라저래라 하는 것을 더 이상 못 참겠어.
sentences.note:
- **have had enough of** sb/sth: ~ 을 더 이상 못 참다
- **boss** sb **around**: ~ 에게 이래라저래라 하다

sentences.text: Can I get a discount?
What's your price range?
It's too expensive.
It's more expensive than I thought.
That's out of my price range.
I can't afford that.
This is all I have.
I don't have enough money.
Can you come down a little?
Can you give me a discount?
What's your best price?
How much lower can you go?
sentences.ko: 얼마나 더 깎아 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Can you give me a discount for cash?
Is this cheaper if I pay with cash?
If I pay in cash, can you lower the price?
sentences.ko: 현금으로 내면 가격을 좀 낮춰 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Is Jason off today? He’s not answering the phone.
sentences.ko: 오늘 제이슨 휴무인가요? 전화를 안 받네요.
sentences.note: - **be off**: 휴무이다

sentences.text: He has gone for the day for a family emergency.
sentences.note: - **have gone for the day**: 이미 퇴근했다

sentences.text: Thank you for the information.
I’m in charge of this project, so you can tell me.
sentences.note: - **be in charge of** sth: ~ 을 담당하다(책임지다)

sentences.text: Sorry to bother you, but can you do me a favor?
sentences.ko: 귀찮게 해서 죄송한데, 부탁 하나 들어 줄래요?
sentences.note:
- **Sorry to bother you**: 귀찮게 해서 죄송해요
- **do** sb **a favor**: ~ 의 부탁을 들어주다

sentences.text: Sure thing. What do you need?
sentences.note: - **Sure thing**: 물론이죠

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 해 본 지 정말 오래됐어
sentences.text: We finally got together. Let’s go bowling.
sentences.note: - **get together**: 모이다(만나다)

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 해 본 지 정말 오래됐어
sentences.text: I suck at bowling. I haven’t done it for ages.
sentences.ko: 나 볼링을 정말 못해. 안 한 지 오래됐어.
sentences.note:
- **suck at** sth: ~ 를 정말 못하다
- **haven’t done** sth **for ages**: ~ 안 한 지 오래되었다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 해 본 지 정말 오래됐어
sentences.text: Don't be such a crybaby. I’ll go easy on you.
sentences.note:
- **Don’t be such a crybaby**: 엄살 좀 피우지 마
- **go easy on** sb: ~ 를 봐주다 | ~ 에게 살살하다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 해 본 지 정말 오래됐어
sentences.text: I threw a bunch of gutter balls last time.
sentences.note: - **threw a gutter ball**: 도랑으로 빠뜨리다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 해 본 지 정말 오래됐어
sentences.text: The losing team pays for the game. OK?
sentences.note: - **pay for the game**: 게임비를 내다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 해 본 지 정말 오래됐어
sentences.text: Good. Let’s have a practice round before we make teams.
sentences.ko: 좋아. 팀을 나누기 전에 연습경기를 하자.
sentences.note:
- **have a practice round**: 연습경기를 하다
- **make teams**: 팀을 나누다

sentences.text: This is my last offer.
I'll think about it. Thank you.
That's a good price.
That's a steal.
It's a very good price.
We're selling at a loss.
I'll give you a 20% discount.
We'll match that price.
That's my final offer.
That's my final price.
I can't come down anymore.
I have a discount coupon.
Can I use this coupon?
I'll come back later.
I'll look around and come back.
Wake up, sleepyhead! You sleep in every day.
sentences.note: - **sleep in**: (일부러) 늦잠 자다

sentences.text: I tossed and turned all night. I couldn’t sleep a wink.
sentences.note:
- **toss and turn**: (잠 못 들고) 뒤척이다
- **couldn’t sleep a wink**: 한숨도 못 잤다

sentences.text: I’m wondering if you can make it on time for school.
sentences.ko: 학교에 제 시간에 도착할 수 있을지 모르겠다.
sentences.note: - **make it on time**: 제 시간에 도착하다

sentences.text: I’m in the middle of washing my hair already.
sentences.note: - **be in the middle of** V-ing(N): ~ 하는 중이다

sentences.text: You’re the black sheep of our family.
Come on. I just forgot to set the alarm.
sentences.ko: 왜 그래요. 알람 맞추는 걸 깜빡했어요.
sentences.note: - **set the alarm**: 알람을 맞추다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 얼굴에 뭐가 나서 신경 쓰여
sentences.text: It bothers me that my face breaks out.
sentences.ko: 얼굴에 (피부) 트러블이 생기는 것이 마음에 걸려.
sentences.note:
- **It bothers me that** S V: ~ 가 마음에 걸리다
- **break out**: (피부) 트러블이 생기다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 얼굴에 뭐가 나서 신경 쓰여
sentences.text: What do you say to getting a facial on Saturday?
sentences.ko: 토요일에 얼굴 마사지를 받으러 가는 건 어때?
sentences.note:
- **What do you say to** V-ing: ~ 하는 건 어때?
- **get a facial**: 얼굴 마사지를 받다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 얼굴에 뭐가 나서 신경 쓰여
sentences.text: Sounds great! What time shall we meet?
sentences.note:
- (That) **sounds great!**: 그거 좋지!
- **What time shall we meet?**: 몇 시에 만날까?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 얼굴에 뭐가 나서 신경 쓰여
sentences.text: Let’s meet at 2 o’clock. How does that sound?
sentences.note: - **How does** sth **sound?**: ~ 는 어때?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 얼굴에 뭐가 나서 신경 쓰여
sentences.text: Good! By the way, how much does it cost?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 얼굴에 뭐가 나서 신경 쓰여
sentences.text: It won’t cost you a lot of money.
sentences.note: - **cost** sb **a lot of money**: 돈이 많이 들다

sentences.text: Is this on sale?
It's 20% off.
Can I get a free sample?
sentences.ko: 무료 샘플 하나 받을 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Take one for free.
We're giving these away.
Buy one and get one free.
I'll take this.
I'd like to buy this one.
I'd like three of these.
Are you having a sale now?
These items are on sale.
We're having a clearance sale.
What are your business hours?
What time do you close?
How late are you open?
I’m really out of shape. I keep on gaining weight.
sentences.note:
- **be out of shape**: 몸매가 망가지다 | 건강이 좋지 않다
- **gain/lose weight**: 체중이 늘다/줄다

sentences.text: Speaking of which, I’ve started working out at the gym.
sentences.ko: 말이 나와서 말인데, 나 헬스장에서 운동하기 시작했어.
sentences.note:
- **speaking of which**: 말이 나와서 말인데
- **work out**: 운동하다

sentences.text: Really? Maybe I should go on a crash diet.
sentences.note: - **go on a crash diet**: 속성 다이어트를 하다

sentences.text: Starving is not helpful. You should go by the book.
sentences.ko: 굶는 건 도움이 안 돼. 원칙대로 해야 해.
sentences.note: - **go by the book**: 원칙대로 하다

sentences.text: Well, I don’t know where to start.
sentences.note: - **don’t know where to start**: 뭐부터 시작할지 모르다

sentences.text: Play it safe, start by joining the gym.
sentences.note: - **play it safe**: 신중을 기하다 | 안전하게 하다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 10년 후에는 뭘 하고 있을 것 같아?
sentences.text: Where do you see yourself in 10 years?
sentences.note:
- **Where do you see yourself?**: 어떤 모습일 것 같나요?
- **in 10 years**: (지금부터) 10년 후에

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 10년 후에는 뭘 하고 있을 것 같아?
sentences.text: I’m not sure, but I’ll be still working here.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 10년 후에는 뭘 하고 있을 것 같아?
sentences.text: I want to start my own business around 50.
sentences.note:
- **start** one’s **own business**: 자신의 사업을 시작하다
- **around 50**: 50살 정도에

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 10년 후에는 뭘 하고 있을 것 같아?
sentences.text: It’s tough to start from scratch again.
sentences.note: - **start** (sth) **from scratch**: 처음부터 시작하다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 10년 후에는 뭘 하고 있을 것 같아?
sentences.text: I’d like to run a small restaurant sometime.
sentences.note: - **run a restaurant**: 식당을 운영하다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 10년 후에는 뭘 하고 있을 것 같아?
sentences.text: Awesome! I’m jealous of people with dreams.
sentences.ko: 멋진데! 난 꿈이 있는 사람들이 부러워.
sentences.note: - **be jealous of** sb: ~가 부러워

sentences.text: Hello, can I help you?
I bought this yesterday, but it doesn't work.
sentences.ko: 어제 이걸 샀는데 작동을 안 해요.

sentences.text: I'd like to exchange this, please.
Can I exchange it for another one?
Can I change the size?
I'd like to return this.
Where should I go to return this?
It doesn't work properly.
It's the wrong size.
The size doesn't fit me.
It's damaged here.
I found a stain here.
I didn't notice when I bought it.
Is there an extra charge?
I'll pay the difference.
You look worried. What’s bothering you?
sentences.ko: 너 걱정 있어 보여. 무슨 고민 있어?
sentences.note: - **What’s bothering you?**: 무슨 고민 있어?(상대방의 표정이 심각해 보일 때 걱정스럽게 물어보는 표현)

sentences.text: I think I’m feeling a little left out at work.
sentences.ko: 회사에서 소외감을 좀 느끼는 것 같아.
sentences.note: - **feel left out**: 소외감을 느끼다 | 왕따가 된 기분이다

sentences.text: Don’t be frustrated. Time heals all wounds.
sentences.note: - **Time heals all wounds**: 시간이 약이야

sentences.text: Will you back me up when I talk in the meeting?
sentences.ko: 회의 때 내가 얘기하면 맞장구 좀 쳐 줄래?
sentences.note: - **back** sb **up**: ~ 를 지지하다

sentences.text: Don’t worry. It’s nothing.
sentences.note: - **It’s nothing**: 별거 아니야

sentences.text: I can’t thank you enough.
sentences.note: - **I can’t thank you enough**: 정말 고마워

sentences.text: Did you walk the dog this morning?
sentences.note: - **walk the dog**: 개를 산책시키다

sentences.text: No. I’m taking her to the vet for grooming.
sentences.ko: 아니. 동물 병원에 데려가서 (동물의) 털 손질 시키려고.
sentences.note:
- **take** one’s **pet to the vet**: ~ 을 동물 병원에 데려가다
- **vet**: 동물 병원(veterinary clinic)
- **grooming**: (동물의) 털 손질

sentences.text: She needs to get a vaccination this time.
sentences.note: - **get a vaccination**: 예방 접종을 받다

sentences.text: By the way, I can’t seem to find her leash.
I took it out of my car for sure yesterday.
sentences.note: - **take** sth **out of** ~: ~을 ~에서 꺼내다

sentences.text: I’ll look for it after putting on my makeup.
sentences.note: - **put on** (one’s) **makeup**: 화장하다

sentences.text: Can I get a refund for this?
Do you have your receipt?
I'd like a refund, please.
I'd like to get a refund for this.
I haven't used it at all.
Can I have the receipt?
Here is my receipt.
I lost my receipt.
I'm afraid I didn't bring the receipt.
No receipt, no refund.
Did you pay in cash or by credit card?
I paid by credit card.
No refund, exchange only.
It's not our policy to give refunds.
sentences.ko: 환불해 드리는 것은 저희 규정이 아닙니다.

sentences.text: How about a little hair of the dog?
sentences.note: - **hair of the dog**: 해장술

sentences.text: Sorry, but I think I’ll pass tonight.
sentences.note: - **I think I’ll pass**: 사양할게(상대방의 권유를 사양할 때 쓰는 표현)

sentences.text: You promised to treat this time. You have a lot of nerve.
sentences.ko: 이번에 네가 사기로 했잖아. 정말 뻔뻔하네.
sentences.note: - **have a lot of nerve**: 정말 뻔뻔하다

sentences.text: Something urgent came up suddenly.
sentences.note: - **Something comes up**: (무슨) 일이 생기다

sentences.text: You’re so cheap and unreliable.
sentences.ko: 넌 정말 인색하고(치사하고), 믿을 수가 없어.

sentences.text: Sorry. I have a sore throat. Let’s go out next week.
sentences.ko: 미안. 목이 너무 아파서 그래. 다음 주에 하자.
sentences.note: - **have a sore throat**: 목이 아프다

sentences.text: I don’t know how to put it into words.
sentences.note: - **put** sth **into words**: 말로 표현하다

sentences.text: I’ve got a bad feeling. Just get to the point.
sentences.ko: 느낌이 안 좋은데. 그냥 요점만 말해.
sentences.note:
- **have got a bad feeling**: 느낌이 안 좋다
- **get to the point**: 요점만 말하다

sentences.text: I guess this is it. We are so different.
sentences.ko: 이게 끝인가 봐. 우린 서로 너무 달라.
sentences.note: - **I guess this is it**: 이게 끝인가 봐

sentences.text: I think we need to relax and take it slow.
