sentences.note: - **have a long-distance relationship**: 장거리 연애를 하다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 점심 먹으며 얘기 좀 하자
sentences.text: Yes, it’s tough. Let’s catch up over lunch.
sentences.ko: 응, 힘드네. 점심을 먹으며 밀린 얘기를 좀 하자.
sentences.note:
- **tough**: 힘든
- **catch up over** 음식(음료): ~ 을 먹으며(마시며) 밀린 얘기를 하다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 점심 먹으며 얘기 좀 하자
sentences.text: Let’s go grab something you like.
sentences.note: - **go grab** sth: ~ 을 먹으러 가다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 점심 먹으며 얘기 좀 하자
sentences.text: How about the Kimchi stew place across the street?
sentences.note:
- **Kimchi stew place**: 김치찌개 집
- **across the street**: 길 건너에

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 점심 먹으며 얘기 좀 하자
sentences.text: Are you okay with spicy food? Let’s go.
sentences.note: - **Are you okay with** sth?: ~ 인데 괜찮겠어?

sentences.text: You look great in this picture.
Thanks, I love it.
Did they come out all right?
This photo came out very well.
You're very photogenic.
I look terrible in pictures.
You look better in person.
You look much better in real life.
You look better than in real life.
I'm sorry, but I'm camera-shy.
sentences.ko: 미안하지만 전 사진 찍히는 걸 쑥스러워해요.

sentences.text: I don't like being photographed.
sentences.ko: 전 사진 찍히는 걸 안 좋아해요.

sentences.text: The picture is blurry.
The picture is out of focus.
Let’s make a toast to your success. Bottoms up!
sentences.ko: 너의 성공을 위해 건배하자. 원 샷!
sentences.note: - **make a toast**: 건배하다

sentences.text: I must not drink today. I’m on medication.
sentences.ko: 오늘 나 술 마시면 안 돼. 약을 복용 중이거든.
sentences.note: - **be on medication**: (약을) 복용 중이다

sentences.text: Come on. I’m not falling for that trick.
sentences.ko: 왜 이래. 그런 속임수에 안 속아.
sentences.note: - **fall for** sb/sth: ~에 속다 | ~에게 반하다

sentences.text: I have a bad cold and ache all over.
sentences.note: - **ache all over**: 온몸이 쑤시다

sentences.text: Why don’t you take a day off and relax?
sentences.ko: 하루 휴가 내고, 좀 쉬지 그래?
sentences.note: - **take a day off**: 하루 휴가 내다(쉬다)

sentences.text: I’d love to, but I’m tied up at work.
sentences.note: - **be tied up**: 바쁘다

sentences.text: I got an invitation to my college reunion.
sentences.note: - **get an invitation to** V(N): 초대를 받다

sentences.text: That brings me back. We had a ball back then.
sentences.ko: 옛날 생각난다. 그 시절엔 즐거운 시간을 보냈지.
sentences.note:
- **That brings me back**: 옛날 생각난다
- **have a ball**: 즐거운 시간을 보내다
- **back then**: 그 시절엔

sentences.text: I’m a little depressed. It just makes me feel old.
sentences.ko: 기분이 안 좋네. 나이가 든 것 같아서.
sentences.note: - **It makes** sb **feel** Adj**: ~ 라는 느낌이 들다

sentences.text: Don’t take it seriously. Look how well you’re doing.
sentences.ko: 심각하게 받아들이지 마. 얼마나 잘 살고 있는지 봐라.
sentences.note:
- **Don’t take it seriously**: 심각하게 받아들이지마
- **Look how** Adj(Adv) S V: 얼마나 ~ 하는지 봐라

sentences.text: I wonder how much they’ve changed.
Have fun catching up with everybody.
sentences.ko: 밀린 얘기를 하며 좋은 시간 보내.
sentences.note: - **catch up with** sb: ~ 와 밀린 얘기를 하다

sentences.text: Can I book a table for three at 6?
Can I have your name, please?
I'd like to book a table for two.
I'd like to book a table at 7.
I'd like to make a reservation for five.
Do you have a table for five at 6:30?
I'd like to book a table for two at 8.
For how many, ma'am?
How many in your party?
Five people at 2 p.m.
Two adults and two children.
Two adults and one child.
There are four of us.
There are four including me.
How did you get into an accident?
sentences.note: - **get into an accident**: 사고를 당하다

sentences.text: A man crashed into my car and ran away.
sentences.ko: 어떤 남자가 내 차에 충돌하고 도망갔어.
sentences.note: - **crash into** sth: ~에 충돌하다

sentences.text: That was close. Did you figure out who did that?
sentences.ko: 큰일 날 뻔했네. 누가 그랬는지 밝혀냈어?
sentences.note: - **That was close**: 큰일 날 뻔했다

sentences.text: Yes. But he was trying to put the blame on me.
sentences.ko: 응. 근데 그 사람이 나한테 책임을 돌렸어.
sentences.note: - **put the blame on** sb: ~의 탓으로 돌리다

sentences.text: You’re out of luck today. Hope it works out for you.
sentences.ko: 오늘 운이 없었구나. (일이) 잘 되길 바래.
sentences.note:
- **be out of luck**: 운이 없다
- **work out**: (일이) 잘 되다

sentences.text: I was so upset. I almost burst into tears.
sentences.note: - **burst into tears**: 울음을 터트리다

sentences.text: Where are you off to in such a hurry?
sentences.note:
- **Where are you off to?**: 어디 가는 길이야?
- **in such a hurry**: 급하게

sentences.text: I’m going out for an annual family gathering.
sentences.note: - **annual family gathering**: 연례 가족 모임

sentences.text: Your family members have a strong bond with each other.
sentences.note: - **have a strong bond** (with): (~ 와) 유대 관계가 좋다

sentences.text: My mom always nags me about not getting married.
sentences.ko: 엄마는 결혼 안하는 것에 대해 언제나 잔소리해.
sentences.note: - **nag** sb **about** sth(V-ing): ~ 에 대해 잔소리하다

sentences.text: You should put yourself in her place.
sentences.note: - **put oneself in** one’s **place(shoes)**: ~ 의 입장이 되어 생각하다

sentences.text: I’ve put a lot of effort into that, but I’m getting nowhere with it.
sentences.note:
- **put a lot of effort** (into sth): ~ 에 노력을 많이 하다
- **get nowhere** (with sb/sth): ~ 에 진전(성과)이 없다

sentences.text: I'd like to reserve a table for tonight.
I'm sorry, but we're fully booked.
What time will you come?
What time will you be arriving?
We're fully booked for tonight.
We're booked up for tonight.
We're fully booked at that time.
I'm afraid we're full now.
All seats are reserved.
Would you like to wait?
You should wait at least 20 minutes.
I'd like to confirm my reservation.
I want to change my reservation.
I'm afraid I have to cancel my reservation.
sentences.ko: 죄송하지만 예약을 취소해야 할 것 같습니다.

sentences.text: I'd like to reschedule my reservation.
Have you made a profit on your house?
sentences.note: - **make a profit**: 수익을 내다

sentences.text: Just getting by. I just broke even.
sentences.note: - **broke even**: 본전이다

sentences.text: I’m thinking of taking out a loan from the bank.
sentences.note: - **take out a loan**: 대출을 받다

sentences.text: Can you recommend a new area to invest in?
I have my own problems. I’m busy paying off a debt.
sentences.ko: 내 코가 석 자야. 빚 갚느라 정신없어.
sentences.note:
- **have** one's **own problems**: 내 코가 석 자다
- **pay off a debt**: 빚을 갚다(청산하다)

sentences.text: We’re in the same boat. I’m struggling to raise money.
sentences.ko: 우린 같은 처지네. 나도 돈 모으려 애쓰고 있어.
sentences.note:
- **be in the same boat**: 같은 처지이다
- **raise money**: 돈을 마련하다

sentences.text: I got an electric car. It’s called Model Y.
It’s cool. It must’ve cost you a fortune.
sentences.note: - **cost** (sb) **a fortune**: 큰 돈이 들다

sentences.text: EVs will become the norm in the near future.
sentences.note:
- **become the norm**: 대세가 되다
- **in the near future**: 머지않아

sentences.text: Many countries will ban the sale of new fossil-fuel cars from 2030.
sentences.ko: 많은 나라가 2030년부터 새로운 내연기관 차량 판매를 금지한대.
sentences.note:
- **ban** sth: ~ 을 금지하다
- **fossil-fuel cars**: 내연기관 차량

sentences.text: Tesla is paving the way for an era of EVs.
sentences.ko: 테슬라가 전기차 시대를 위해 앞장서고 있어.
sentences.note: - **pave the way for** sb/sth: ~를 위해 앞장서다(길을 닦다)

sentences.text: They have built a loyal fan base globally.
sentences.note: - **build a** (loyal) **fan base**: (충성스러운) 팬층을 구축하다

sentences.text: Do you have a reservation?
I made a reservation for five.
We have a reservation at 7:00.
May I have your name, please?
Please come this way.
Let me show you to your table.
We don't have a reservation.
I didn't make a reservation.
Do you have a table for two?
Table for three, please.
Can I have a table by the window?
I'd like to sit by the window.
Please wait to be seated.
Can you put these tables together?
sentences.ko: 이 테이블들을 붙여 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Can we move to a different table?
I heard your wife was hospitalized last night.
sentences.note: - **be hospitalized**: (병원에) 입원하다

sentences.text: She was in a coma when she was taken to the ER.
sentences.note:
- **be in a coma**: 혼수상태이다
- **be taken to** 장소: ~ 로 데려가다
- **ER**: 응급실(Emergency Room)

sentences.text: I hope she’ll be released from the hospital soon.
sentences.ko: 그녀가 곧 퇴원할 수 있기를 바래.
sentences.note: - **be released from the hospital**: (병원에서) 퇴원하다

sentences.text: After the surgery, she is in stable condition now.
sentences.note: - **be in stable condition**: 안정된 상태이다

sentences.text: What did the doctor say? Is she all right?
He said she should bring her cholesterol level down.
sentences.note: - **bring** sth **down**: ~ 을 낮추다(떨어뜨리다)

sentences.text: Mom! Did you put my phone away?
sentences.note: - **put** sth **away**: ~ 을 치우다

sentences.text: Keep looking. It must be somewhere.
Please don’t tell me you’ve hidden it.
sentences.note: - **Don’t tell me** S V: 설마 ~ 하는 건 아니겠지?

sentences.text: You catch on quick. How did you pick up on that?
sentences.note:
- **catch on quick**: 눈치(이해)가 빠르다
- **pick up on** sth: 알아차리다(간파하다)

sentences.text: I can tell right away. It’s written on your face.
sentences.ko: 보면 바로 알아차리죠. 얼굴에 쓰여 있어요.
sentences.note:
- **tell**: 알아차리다
- **be written on** one's **face**: 얼굴에 쓰여 있다

sentences.text: Your battery was dead. So, I’m charging it.
sentences.note:
- one’s **battery is(go) dead**: 배터리가 떨어지다
- **charge** sth: ~ 을 충전하다

sentences.text: Are you ready to order?
Can you wait for a minute?
Menu, please.
Can I have the menu, please?
Can I take your order?
Would you like to order now?
I'm not ready to order.
We need a little more time.
We need a few more minutes.
We haven't decided yet.
Take your time. I'll come back.
We are ready to order.
Are you waiting for someone?
We're expecting three more people.
I'm waiting for someone else.
Congratulations! Your book is selling like hotcakes.
sentences.ko: 축하해요! 당신 책이 불티나게 팔리고 있어요.
sentences.note: - **sell like hotcakes**: 불티나게 팔리다

sentences.text: Thanks. Please spread the word for me.
sentences.note: - **spread the word**: 입소문을 내다

sentences.text: Sure. You have a way to promote it to the public?
sentences.note: - **promote to the public**: 대중에게 홍보하다

sentences.text: Yes. I’ve been posting free lectures on my site.
sentences.ko: 네. 제 (인터넷) 사이트에 무료 강의를 올리고 있어요.
sentences.note: - **post** sth **on the site**: (인터넷) 사이트에 ~ 을 올리다

sentences.text: I’ll put in a good word to my friends and acquaintances.
sentences.ko: 제도 친구들과 지인들한테 얘기를 잘 해 줄게요.
sentences.note: - **put in a good word**: 애기(말)를 잘 해 주다

sentences.text: Thanks a million. That means a lot to me.
sentences.ko: 정말 감사해요. 정말 큰 힘이 돼요.
sentences.note:
- **Thanks a million**: 정말 고마워요
- **That means a lot to me**: 나에게 큰 의미가 있다

sentences.text: What are you up to tonight?
sentences.note: - **What are you up to?**: 뭐 할거야(뭐하고 지내)?

sentences.text: Nothing much. Maybe I’ll be working like a dog.
sentences.note:
- **Nothing much**: 별일 없어
- **work like a dog**: 열심히 일하다

sentences.text: All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy.
sentences.ko: 일만 하고 놀지 않으면 바보가 돼.

sentences.text: I know. But we’re always short-handed.
sentences.note: - **short-handed**: 일손이 부족한

sentences.text: Besides, we don’t get paid extra for overtime.
sentences.ko: 게다가, 초과 근무수당도 충분히 못 받잖아.
sentences.note: - **get paid extra for overtime**: 초과 근무수당을 받다

sentences.text: It burns me up. I’m having a mental breakdown.
sentences.note:
- **It burns me up** (to V): (~ 하고 보니) 열 받네
- **have a mental breakdown**: (정신적으로) 충격이 크다

sentences.text: What do you recommend?
How about the New York steak?
What's good here?
What's your specialty here?
What do you recommend?
Do you have any suggestions?
What's today's special?
Do you have a lunch special?
What's the best local food?
sentences.ko: 가장 인기 있는 현지 음식은 무엇인가요?

sentences.text: What's the fastest meal?
Would you explain this one?
What kind of dish is this?
What's that dish over there?
What's the main ingredient?
I think it’s too much for me to play golf.
sentences.ko: 나한텐 골프가 너무 어려운 것 같아.
sentences.note: - sth **is too much for** sb: ~ 이 ~ 에게 너무 어렵다(벅차다)

sentences.text: Once you get the hang of it, it’s just a matter of time.
sentences.note:
- **get the hang of** sth: 요령이 생기다
- **a matter of time**: 시간문제

sentences.text: Would it be possible to catch up with you in a year?
sentences.ko: 1년 안에 네 실력을 따라잡는 게 가능할까?
sentences.note: - **catch up with** sth/sb: ~ 을 따라잡다

sentences.text: I guess so. For starters, try to get used to it.
sentences.note:
- **For starters**: 우선은
- **get used to** sth: ~ 에 익숙해지다

sentences.text: All the practice will pay off in the near future.
sentences.ko: 열심히 연습하면 조만간 성과가 있을 거야.
sentences.note: - **pay off**: 성과가 있다

sentences.text: It’s always easier said than done.
sentences.note: - **easier said than done**: 말은 행동보다 쉽다

sentences.text: I think I pulled a muscle in my neck.
sentences.note: - **pull a muscle in** (신체 부위): ~ 을 삐끗하다

sentences.text: I told you to stretch as often as possible.
sentences.ko: 스트레칭을 가능한 한 자주 하라고 했잖아.
sentences.note: - **as often as possible**: 가능한 한 자주

sentences.text: I’m going to take a Pilates class like you.
sentences.note: - **take a Pilates class**: 필라테스 강습을 받다

sentences.text: Good thinking, but you shouldn’t rush into it.
sentences.note:
- **Good thinking**: 잘 생각했어
- **rush into** sth: ~을 서두르다 | 성급하게 행동하다

sentences.text: I can’t be bothered to do anything because I feel under the weather.
sentences.note:
- **I can’t be bothered to** V | **with** N: ~ 하기 | ~ 이 귀찮다
- **feel under the weather**: 몸이 안 좋다

sentences.text: Try to keep exercising and stay in shape.
sentences.note: - **stay in shape**: 건강(몸매)을 유지하다

sentences.text: What would you like?
I'd like seafood spaghetti.
What would you like to have?
I don't know what to order.
Okay, I'll have that.
I'll take this one.
I'll have the same.
Make it two, please.
I'll have what they're having.
sentences.ko: 저 사람들이 먹고 있는 걸로 주세요.

sentences.text: I'd like to have some local food.
Anything to drink?
Anything else?
Will that be all?
That's all for now.
Hey, I’m back. What did I miss?
sentences.ko: 이봐. 나 돌아왔어. (나 없을 때) 무슨 얘기 했어?
sentences.note: - **What did I miss?**: (나 없을 때) 무슨 얘기 했어?

sentences.text: Guess what I just heard? Take a guess.
sentences.ko: 방금 무슨 얘기 들은 줄 알아? 대충 맞춰 봐.
sentences.note: - **take a guess**: 대충 맞추다

sentences.text: What do you take me for? Give it to me straight.
sentences.ko: 날 뭘로 보는 거야? 솔직히 말해.
sentences.note:
- **What do you take me for?**: 날 뭘로 보는 거야?
- **Give it to me straight**: 솔직히 말해

sentences.text: They got carried away and kissed each other.
sentences.note: - **get carried away**: 흥분하다(자재력을 잃다)

sentences.text: I knew it! They were drinking a lot.
sentences.ko: 그럴 줄 알았어! 술 엄청 마셔대더니.
sentences.note: - **I knew it!**: 그럴 줄 알았어!

sentences.text: I think they’re made for each other.
sentences.note: - **be made for each other**: 천생연분이다

sentences.text: I was told that Tom got a divorce.
sentences.note:
- **I was told that** ~: ~ 라고 듣다
- **get a divorce**: 이혼하다

sentences.text: No kidding! They have been separated.
sentences.note: - **be separated**: 별거하다

sentences.text: They walked down the aisle just months ago.
sentences.note: - **walk down the aisle**: 결혼하다

sentences.text: I can't believe that. You live and learn.
sentences.ko: 믿을 수가 없어. 별일이 다 있네.
sentences.note: - **live and learn**: 별일이 다 있다

sentences.text: It really gets me down. I don’t know how I can comfort him.
sentences.ko: 정말 나를 우울하게 하네. 어떻게 그를 위로해 줘야 하나.
sentences.note:
- **get** sb **down**: ~ 을 우울하게 하다
- **comfort** sb: ~ 를 위로하다

sentences.text: Me neither. I fell out of touch with him recently.
sentences.ko: 나도 그래. 최근 그와 연락이 끊겼거든.
sentences.note: - **fall out of touch with** sb: ~ 와 연락이 끊기다

sentences.text: I don't think I ordered this.
sentences.ko: 제가 주문한 게 아닌 것 같은데요.

What happened to my order?
My order hasn't come yet.
How much longer is the wait?
Please rush my order.
Have you been helped?
We've been waiting for 30 minutes.
Sorry to keep you waiting.
Can you wait for about 20 minutes?
Can I speak with the manager, please?
I didn't order this.
This is not what I ordered.
Can I change my order?
Could you clear the table, please?

sentences.ko: 이 사진에 당신은 잘 나오지 않았네요.
sentences.note: - **come out great**: (사진이) 잘 나오다

sentences.text: To be honest, I’m a little camera-shy.
sentences.ko: 솔직히 전 사진 찍히기 좀 싫어해요.
sentences.note: - **camera-shy**: 사진 찍히기 싫어하는

sentences.text: You look better than your picture.
sentences.note: - **look better than** sth: ~ 보다 나아 보인다

sentences.text: That’s what everybody tells me.
You’d better change your mind and have confidence.
sentences.note:
- **change** one’s **mind**: ~ 의 생각을 바꾸다
- **have confidence**: 자신감을 갖다

sentences.text: On second thought, you have a point.
sentences.ko: 다시 생각해 보니, 당신이 맞는 것 같아요.
sentences.note:
- **on second thought**: 다시 생각해 보니
- **have a point**: ~ 이 맞는 것 같다 | 일리가 있다

sentences.text: Why are you biting your nails?
sentences.note: - **bite** one's **nails**: 손톱을 물어뜯다

sentences.text: Well, I quit smoking cold turkey a few days ago.
sentences.note: - **quit** (sth) **cold turkey**: (나쁜 습관을) 갑자기 끊다

sentences.text: You’re having withdrawal symptoms. Keep up the good work.
sentences.note:
- **withdrawal symptoms**: 금단현상
- **keep up the good work**: 계속 열심히 해

sentences.text: You’re in no place to talk to me like that.
sentences.note: - **be in no place to** V: ~ 할 처지(입장)은 아니다

sentences.text: You got me. I’ll give up smoking soon.
sentences.ko: 할 말이 없네. 나도 곧 담배를 끊을거야.
sentences.note:
- **You got me**: 할 말이 없네
- **give up** V-ing: ~를 끊다(포기하다)

sentences.text: I’m going to give it a try. I’ll try anything.
sentences.note: - **give it a try**: 한번 해 보다

sentences.text: Can I have an extra plate, please?
sentences.ko: 접시 하나 더 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Sure, here you are.
Can I have some more water, please?
sentences.ko: 물 좀 더 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: More water, please.
Can I get some wet tissues?
I dropped my fork.
I dropped my spoon.
Can I get a new one?
Can I have another one?
Can I have a small plate?
sentences.ko: 앞접시(작은 접시) 하나 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Can I have two extra plates?
sentences.ko: 접시 두 개 더 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Can I have more sauce?
sentences.ko: 소스 좀 더 주실 수 있나요?

sentences.text: Can I have some napkins?
Could you take the dishes away?
Can we have a high chair?
sentences.ko: 유아용 식사 의자 좀 주실 수 있나요?

lessons.title: 컨디션 안 좋은 날 | 스테이크 주문

sentences.text: Can I help you find something?
I’m wondering if you can give me a discount on this.
sentences.ko: 이거 할인해 주실 수 있는지 아닌지 궁금해요.
sentences.note:
- **wonder if** S V: ~ 인지 아닌지 궁금하다
- **give** sb **a discount**: ~ 에게 할인해 주다

sentences.text: That’s a steal. We’re selling these at cost.
sentences.note:
- **That’s a steal**: 공짜나 다름없다(싸다)
- **sell** sth **at cost**: 원가에(싸게) 팔다

sentences.text: I don’t like to haggle, but it’s way too expensive.
sentences.note: - **haggle**: 흥정하다

sentences.text: Why don’t you try it on for size?
sentences.note: - **try** sth **on**: ~ 을 입어 보다

sentences.text: If you can’t come down, let me sleep on it.
sentences.ko: 깎아 줄 수 없다면, 생각 좀 해 볼게요.
sentences.note:
- **come down**: 가격을 내리다
- **sleep on** sth: ~ 을 다시 생각해 보다

sentences.text: I think your eyes are swollen.
sentences.note: - **swollen**: 부은

sentences.text: I didn’t get a wink of sleep last night.
sentences.note: - **don’t(can’t) get a wink of sleep**: 한숨도 못 자다

sentences.text: Take a quick nap during lunch break.
sentences.note:
- **take a quick nap**: 잠시 눈 좀 붙이다 | 잠시 낮잠을 자다
- **during lunch break**: 점심시간에

sentences.text: Luckily, my boss is on a business trip today.
sentences.note: - **be(go) on a business trip**: 출장 중이다(가다)

sentences.text: But we need to attend a video conference later.
sentences.ko: 근데 우리 나중에 화상회의에 참석해야 해.
sentences.note: - **attend video conference**: 화상회의에 참석하다

sentences.text: I’m not myself today. It’s going to be a long day.
sentences.ko: 나 오늘 제 정신이 아니야. 긴 하루가 되겠군.
sentences.note:
- **be not oneself**: 제 정신이 아니다
- **long day**: 긴 하루(힘든 하루)

sentences.text: How would you like your steak?
Medium, please.
I'll have a T-bone steak.
Well-done, please.
It's still pink.
It's too tough.
It's very tender.
It's undercooked.
It's overcooked.
It's not cooked enough.
It's not warm enough.
We'll make another one right away.
This work is beyond my ability. I’m not sure if I can do it.
sentences.ko: 이 일은 나의 능력 밖이에요. 할 수 있을지 모르겠어요.
sentences.note: - **be beyond** one's **ability**: ~ 의 능력을 넘어서다

sentences.text: Stop beating around the bush. Just get to the point.
sentences.note:
- **beat around the bush**: 돌려 말하다
- **get to the point**: 본론으로 들어가다

sentences.text: I’m pulling my weight. I deserve a raise.
sentences.ko: 전 제 역할을 다하고 있어요. 급여 인상을 받을 만해요.
sentences.note:
- **pull** one’s **weight**: 역할을 다하다
- **deserve** N | **deserve to** V: ~ 받을 만하다 | ~ 할 만한 자격이 있다

sentences.text: Pay raise? Don’t start with that again.
sentences.ko: 급여 인상이라고요? 그 얘긴 꺼내지도 마세요.
sentences.note: - **Don’t start with that**: 그 얘긴 꺼내지도 마

sentences.text: I’m going to put in for a transfer to another division.
sentences.note: - **put in for** sth: ~ 을 신청하다

sentences.text: Please stop pressuring me. You’re driving me crazy.
sentences.ko: 나 그만 괴롭혀요. 당신은 나를 미치게 해요.
sentences.note: - **drive** sb **crazy**: ~ 을 미치게 하다

sentences.text: I was passed over for a promotion.
sentences.note: - **be passed over** (for sth): ~ 에서 제외되다

sentences.text: That’s a shame. Let’s have pork belly with soju.
sentences.note:
- **That’s a shame**: 안타깝다(아쉽다)
- **pork belly with soju**: 삼겹살에 소주

sentences.text: Thanks, but my stomach is bothering me.
sentences.ko: 고맙긴 한데, 위가 나를 불편하게 해.
sentences.note: - sth **is bothering** sb: ~ 를 불편하게 하다

sentences.text: I guess you worry too much about it.
sentences.note: - **worry too much about** sth: ~ 를 크게 신경 쓰다

sentences.text: No. Actually I’m just tired. That’s all.
sentences.ko: 아니야. 사실 조금 피곤해. 그게 다야.

sentences.text: I get the picture. Take care of yourself.
sentences.note:
- **get the picture**: (상황을) 이해하다
- **take care of yourself**: 몸 관리 잘해

sentences.text: Would you like some dessert?
I think I'll pass dessert.
Are you finished?
Would you care for some dessert?
I'd like some dessert, please.
What would you like for dessert?
What do you have?
What do you have for dessert?
I'd like some coffee, please.
I'll have some ice cream, please.
I'd like more coffee, please.
I think I'll skip dessert.
Thanks, but I'll pass.
No, thank you.
Look outside! It’s pouring.
sentences.ko: 바깥 좀 봐! (비가) 억수같이 오고 있어.
sentences.note: - **It’s pouring**: (비가) 억수같이 오다

sentences.text: I don’t feel like cooking. Let’s send out for Chinese food.
sentences.note:
- **don’t feel like** V-ing(N): ~ 하고 싶지 않다
- **send out for** 음식: ~ 을 배달시키다

sentences.text: What’s the weather going to be like tomorrow?
There’s a good chance it will rain in the afternoon.
sentences.note: - **There is a good chance** S V: ~ 할 가능성이 높다

sentences.text: Too bad we have to be cooped up at home on Sunday.
sentences.note:
- **Too bad** S V: ~ 이라서 아쉽다
- **be cooped up** (at/in 장소): (~에) 쳐박혀(갇혀) 있다

sentences.text: Damn it! There goes my weekend.
sentences.note: - **There goes** N: ~ 을 망쳤다(날 샜다)

sentences.text: Hi, dad. Is mom in? It’s mom’s birthday.
sentences.note: - **Is** sb **in?**: ~ 있어요?

sentences.text: It’s so sweet of you to remember. I’ll put her on. (Mother picks up the phone.)
sentences.ko: 기억해 줘서 고맙구나. 엄마에게 전화를 바꿔줄게. (엄마가 전화를 받는다.)
sentences.note:
- **It’s sweet of** sb **to** V**: ~ 해줘서 고마워
- **put** sb **on** (the phone): ~ 에게 전화를 바꿔주다
- **pick up the phone**: 전화를 받다

sentences.text: Hey, honey! It’s been a long time. What’s up?
sentences.note: - **It’s been a long time**: 오랜만이다

sentences.text: Happy birthday, mom. I’ll treat you to dinner tonight. I’m going to drop by after I get off work.
sentences.ko: 생신 축하드려요, 엄마. 오늘 저녁식사를 대접할게요. 퇴근한 후 들를게요.
sentences.note:
- **threat** sb **to** 음식(식사): ~ 를 대접하다
- **drop by**: 들르다
- **get off work**: 퇴근하다

sentences.text: Thanks. We can decide where to go later.
Let's split the bill.
How much is my share?
Check, please.
I'd like the bill, please.
Can I have the check, please?
All together, please.
How much is it all together?
Your total comes to $50.
That'll be $35.20.
Separate checks, please.
Do you take credit cards?
Here you go.
Can you sign here?
Can I have a receipt?

lessons.title: 어깨 통증 | 포장 및 계산 오류

sentences.text: Do you have any big plans this Saturday?
sentences.ko: 이번 주 토요일에 특별한 계획 있어?

sentences.text: I’m afraid I have some work to catch up on.
sentences.ko: 안타깝게도 밀린 일을 좀 만회해야 해.
sentences.note: - **catch up on** sth: (밀린 일을) 만회(보충)하다

sentences.text: You look really stressed out. What happened?
sentences.ko: 너 엄청 스트레스 받아 보여. 무슨 일이야?
sentences.note: - **stressed out**: 스트레스 받은

sentences.text: The last thing I wanna do is fill in for someone.
sentences.ko: 난 절대 다른 사람 일을 대신하고 싶지 않아.
sentences.note:
- **fill in for** sb: ~ 를 대신하다
- **The last thing I wanna do is** V: 절대 ~ 하고 싶지 않다

sentences.text: Stick it out and don’t bite off more than you can chew.
sentences.note: - **bite off more than** sb **can chew**: 무리 하다

sentences.text: I can’t stand the sight of him. Let’s take a walk.
sentences.ko: 그 녀석 꼴도 보기 싫어. 우리 산책하자.
sentences.note: - **can’t stand the sight of** sb/sth: ~ 는 꼴도 보기 싫다

sentences.text: You don’t seem to be feeling well.
My right shoulder hurts like hell. I’m going to take a sick leave for a few days.
sentences.ko: 우측 어깨가 엄청 아파. 며칠 병가를 내려고.
sentences.note:
- sth **hurts like hell**: ~ 가 엄청 아프다
- **take a sick leave**: 병가를 내다

sentences.text: You’ve overworked yourself. Take it easy.
sentences.note:
- **overwork oneself**: 무리하다(과로하다)
- **take it easy**: 쉬엄쉬엄하다

sentences.text: Talk is cheap. I almost missed a deadline.
sentences.ko: 말은 쉽지. 마감일을 거의 놓칠 뻔 했어.
sentences.note:
- **Talk is cheap**: 말은 쉽다
- **miss a deadline**: 마감일을 놓치다

sentences.text: Lighten up. That’s the way it goes.
sentences.note:
- **Lighten up**: 기운 내
- **That’s the way** sth **goes**: ~ 이란 그런거야

sentences.text: Thanks. You’re the best.
Can I have a doggy bag, please?
sentences.ko: 남은 음식을 싸 갈 봉투 좀 주시겠어요?

sentences.text: I'll have that ready in a minute.
Can you wrap this up, please?
Can I have a doggy bag, please?
sentences.ko: 남은 음식을 싸 갈 봉투 좀 주시겠어요?

sentences.text: Doggy bag, please.
Please pack them separately.
There seems to be a mistake.
There is a mistake in the bill.
I'm afraid the check is wrong.
What's this amount for?
I think I got the wrong change.
I'm afraid you gave me the wrong change.
Is the tip included?
Does this include the tip?
Does the price include tax?
Would you mind backing up a little, please?
sentences.note:
- **Would you mind** V-ing: ~ 해 주실래요?
- **back up**: 후진하다

sentences.text: What’s the matter? I always park here.
This is a tow-away zone. You can get a parking ticket.
sentences.ko: 여기는 (불법 주차) 견인지역이에요. 주차 위반 딱지를 받을 수 있어요.
sentences.note: - **get a parking ticket**: 주차 위반 딱지를 받다

sentences.text: Don’t make a big deal out of nothing.
sentences.ko: 별거 아닌 일로 호들갑을 떨지 마세요.
sentences.note: - **make a big deal**: 호들갑을 떨다 | 소란을 피우다

sentences.text: As far as I know, there’s a parking lot behind the building.
sentences.ko: 내가 알기로는, 건물 뒤에 주차장이 있어요.
sentences.note: - **as far as I know**: 내가 알기로는

sentences.text: That’s news to me. Thanks for the tip.
sentences.note:
- **That’s news to me**: 금시초문이다
- **Thanks for the tip**: 알려 줘서 고마워(도움이 되는 정보를 알려줘서 고맙다고 말할 때 사용하는 표현)

sentences.text: Have you packed everything? Hop in!
sentences.note: - **hop in** (the car): (차에) 타다

sentences.text: Dad, will you drop by the rest area?
I can see right through you. You want to have snacks.
sentences.ko: 너의 속셈을 알 수 있어. 군것질하고 싶구나.
sentences.note:
- **see right through** sb: ~ 의 속셈을 알 수 있다 | ~ 를 꿰뚫어 보다
- **have snacks**: 군것질하다

sentences.text: Don’t get me wrong. I don’t take the easy way out.
sentences.ko: 오해하지 마세요. 잔머리를 쓰는 거 아니에요.
sentences.note:
- **Don’t get me wrong**: 오해하지 마세요
- **take the easy way out**: 잔머리를 쓰다 | 쉬운 길을 선택하다

sentences.text: I’m just joking. I’m always behind you.
sentences.note: - **be behind** sb: ~ 를 지지하다 | ~ 의 배후에 있다

sentences.text: You made my day. Let’s get a move on.
sentences.ko: 아빠는 나를 기쁘게 해요. 어서 가요.
sentences.note:
- **make** one’s **day**: ~ 은 ~ 를 기쁘게 하다
- **get a move on**: 어서 가다(서두르다)

sentences.text: For here or to go?
sentences.ko: 여기서 드실 건가요, 포장해 가실 건가요?

sentences.text: To go, please.
Can I take your order?
Combo number two, please.
I'll have the combo number three, please.
I'll have a burger and fries.
Do you want it to go?
I want it to go, please.
For here, please.
I'll have it here.
Can I get that to go?
Combo number four to go, please.
Two hamburgers to go, please.
Which size would you like?
Large, please.
You look sharp today. What’s going on?
sentences.note: - **look sharp**: (의상이) 멋지다

sentences.text: I treated myself to a new coat behind my wife’s back.
sentences.ko: 아내 몰래 큰맘 먹고 새 코트를 샀어.
sentences.note: - **treat oneself to** sth: 큰맘 먹고 ~ 을 사다

sentences.text: She’ll blow her top if she finds out.
sentences.ko: 네 아내가 알면 불같이 화낼 것 같은데.
sentences.note: - **blow** one’s **top**: 불같이 화내다

sentences.text: Leave it to me. I’ll take care of it.
sentences.ko: 나한테 맡겨. 내가 알아서 할 거야.
sentences.note: - **leave it to** sb/sth: ~ 에게 맡기다

sentences.text: I feel sorry for her. What kind of husband are you?
sentences.ko: 네 아내를 불쌍히 생각해. 무슨 남편이 그러냐?
sentences.note:
- **feel sorry for** sb: ~ 를 불쌍히 생각하다
- **What kind of** sb **are you?**: 무슨 ~ 가 그러냐?

sentences.text: Keep your voice down. Don’t tell a soul.
sentences.ko: 목소리 좀 낮춰. 아무한테도 말하지 마.
sentences.note: - **Don’t tell a soul**: 아무한테도 말하지 마

sentences.text: You have a way with kids. How can you do that?
sentences.note: - **have a way with** sth/sb: ~ 을 잘 다루다

sentences.text: My experience tells me that scolding them is not working.
sentences.ko: 내 경험에 의하면 야단치는 것은 효과가 없어.
sentences.note:
- **My experience tells me that** S V: 내 경험에 의하면 ~ 이다
- **scold**: 야단치다(꾸짖다)
- **work**: 효과가 있다

sentences.text: I need to brush up on my parenting skills.
sentences.note:
- **brush up** (on) sth: ~ 을 연마(복습)하다
- **parenting skill**: 양육 기술

sentences.text: You’re humble. You know better than I.
sentences.ko: 겸손하네. 네가 나보다 더 잘 알잖아.
sentences.note: - **humble**: 겸손한

sentences.text: How about your husband? Is he doing okay?
He’s fine. He doesn’t touch alcohol nowadays.
sentences.ko: 잘 지내. 요즘 술을 입에도 안 대.
sentences.note: - **haven’t touched(don’t touch) alcohol**: 술을 입에도 안 대다

sentences.text: Do you want that with everything?
Hold the onions, please.
Take it easy on the mayo.
Go easy on the onions.
Hold the mayo, please.
Hold the pickles, please.
No ice, please.
No mustard, please.
Can you cut it in half, please?
Please pack them separately.
I'll have a Coke with no ice.
Where are the straws?
Can I get a refill?
Do you have free refills on coffee?
I got a lecture for failing to meet the deadline.
sentences.note:
- **get a lecture**: 야단맞다
- **meet the deadline**: 마감시간을 지키다

sentences.text: You know how your boss is about deadlines.
I don’t talk to let him down any more.
sentences.ko: 이젠 더 이상 그를 실망시키고 싶지 않아.
sentences.note: - **let** sb **down**: ~ 를 실망시키다

sentences.text: Let’s talk about it over a drink tonight.
sentences.note: - **over** 음식(음료): ~ 을 먹으면서(마시면서)

sentences.text: I got paid today. I’ll treat you to dinner.
sentences.ko: 오늘 급여를 받았어. 내가 너에게 저녁 식사를 대접할게.
sentences.note:
- **get paid**: 급여를 받다
- **treat** sb **to** 식사: ~ 에게 식사를 대접하다

sentences.text: I owe you one. It’s my turn to return the favor.
sentences.ko: 너한테 신세진 게 있어. 내가 보답할 차례야.
sentences.note:
- **owe** sb **one**: 신세지다(빚지다)
- **return the favor**: 보답하다

sentences.text: What’s new with you these days?
sentences.note: - **What’s new with you?**: 별일 없어?

sentences.text: I’m biting the bullet. I’ve been stuck in the office.
sentences.ko: 이를 악물고 견디고 있어. 사무실에 갇혀 있었어.
sentences.note:
- **bite the bullet**: 이를 악물고 견디다
- **be stuck in** 장소: ~ 에 갇혀 있다

sentences.text: I’ve been working far away from home for 5 years.
sentences.note: - **work far away from home**: 가족과 떨어져서 일하다

sentences.text: Oh, man! I Know what it’s like to be alone.
sentences.ko: 저런! 혼자 지내는 것이 어떤 건지 알아.
sentences.note: - **know what it’s like to** V: ~ 가 어떤 건지 알다

sentences.text: My wife wants me to take paternity leave.

sentences.ko: 다음에 잘하면 되지. 난 잘 해낸 것 같아.

sentences.note:

sentences.note: - **attend a meeting**: 회의에 참석하다

sentences.note:

- **if possible**: 가능하면(가급적)

sentences.note: - **give** sb **a wake-up call**: ~ 에게 모닝콜 해 주다

sentences.text: I’m so fed up with your service.

sentences.text: I’m happy to get a promotion. I was lucky.
sentences.note:
- **be happy to** V: ~ 하게 되어 기쁘다
- **get a promotion**: 승진하다

sentences.text: Congratulations! you’re qualified for the position.
sentences.ko: 축하해. 넌 그 자리에 대한 자격이 있어.
sentences.note: - **be qualified for** sth: ~ 에 대한 자격이 있다

sentences.text: I didn’t expect too much. Things were not good.
sentences.ko: 기대를 많이 안 했어. 상황이 좋지 않았거든.

sentences.text: I believe you’ll climb the corporate ladder.
sentences.note: - **climb the corporate ladder**: 승진(출세)하다

sentences.text: Easy for you to say. It’s a dog-eat-dog world.
sentences.note:
- **Easy for you to say**: 말이야 쉽지
- **dog-eat-dog world**: 경쟁이 치열한 세상 | 냉혹한 세계

sentences.text: You can say that again. It’s tough to make a living.
sentences.ko: 정말 그래. 생계를 유지하는 것이 쉽지 않아.
sentences.note:
- **You can say that again**: 정말 그래 | 동감이야
- **make a living**: 생계를 유지하다

sentences.text: How often do I take this?
sentences.ko: 이 약은 얼마나 자주 먹어야 하나요?

sentences.text: Three times a day after each meal.
Can you fill this prescription?
Do you have the prescription?
How should I take this medicine?
Can I get some cold medicine?
Do you have anything for a cold?
Do you have anything for a headache?
Do you have any painkillers?
I'd like something for indigestion.
Can I get some digestive medicine?
I need something for motion sickness.
Do you carry sanitary napkins?
Do you have a band-aid?
Who came up with this brilliant idea?
sentences.ko: 누가 이렇게 훌륭한 아이디어를 생각해 냈죠?
sentences.note: - **come up with** sth: ~ 을 생각해 내다

sentences.text: We put our heads together to solve the problem.
sentences.ko: 우리가 머리를 맞대고 상의해, 문제를 해결했어요.
sentences.note: - **put** one’s **heads together**: 머리를 맞대고 상의하다

sentences.text: Good job. Let’s give ourselves a big hand.
sentences.note:
- **Good job**: 잘했어요(훌륭해요)
- **give** sb **a big hand**: ~ 에게 큰 박수를 보내다

sentences.text: Why don’t you report it to the boss right away?
sentences.ko: 사장님께 즉시 보고 드리는 건 어때요?
sentences.note: - **right away**: 즉시(곧바로)

sentences.text: He’s in a bad mood today. Don’t ask for trouble.
sentences.ko: 오늘 기분이 좋지 않으세요. 괜한 짓 하지 마세요.
sentences.note:
- **be in a bad mood**: 기분이 좋지 않다
- **ask for trouble**: 괜한 짓 하다 | 화를 자초하다

sentences.text: Really? I was barking up the wrong tree.
sentences.note: - **bark up the wrong tree**: 헛다리 짚다

sentences.text: You look down. What’s eating you?
sentences.note:
- **look down**: 우울해(침울해) 보이다
- **What’s eating you?**: 무슨 일(고민) 있어?

sentences.text: There was a huge staff reshuffle yesterday.
sentences.note: - **staff reshuffle**: 인사 발령

sentences.text: I don't feel good. What happened?
I got transferred to the China branch.
sentences.note: - **get transferred to** 부서(지역): ~ 로 발령 나다

sentences.text: I'm lost for words. This almost never happens.
sentences.ko: (놀라서) 할 말을 잃었어. 이런 일은 거의 없는데.
sentences.note:
- **be lost for words**: (놀라서) 할 말을 잃다
- **This** (almost) **never happens**: 이런 일은 (거의) 없다

sentences.text: I’m about to pass out. I didn’t sign up for this.
sentences.note:
- **pass out**: 기절하다
- **didn’t sign up for this**: 이러려고 입사한 거 아니다

sentences.text: What seems to be the problem?
I have a bad stomachache.
I'd like to make an appointment.
I'd like to see a doctor.
He is seeing another patient.
sentences.ko: 의사 선생님이 다른 환자를 진료 중이세요.

sentences.text: This is my first visit.
How long do I have to wait?
What are your symptoms?
How long have you been that way?
It's been about 2 days.
Let me check your temperature.
Have you had this before?
Do you have any allergies?
Are you taking any medication?
My father passed away last week.
sentences.note: - **pass away**: 사망하다 | (시간이) 지나가다

sentences.text: I’m so sorry for your loss. I know how you feel.
sentences.ko: 삼가 조의를 표합니다. 어떤 심정인지 알아요.
sentences.note:
- **I’m sorry for your loss**: 삼가 조의를 표합니다
- **know how you feel**: 어떤 기분인지 안다

sentences.text: Thank you for your sympathy.
sentences.note: - **sympathy**: 위로 | 조의(연민)

sentences.text: He was a great man. He had a mind of his own.
sentences.note: - **have a mind of** one’s **own**: 주관이 뚜렷하다

sentences.text: He had to learn the hard way and made it big.
sentences.note:
- **learn the hard way**: 역경(고생)을 통해 배우다
- **make it big**: 크게 성공하다

sentences.text: I’ve looked up to him since I was young.
sentences.note: - **look up to** sb: ~ 를 존경하다

sentences.text: Can I sleep over at Daniel’s place tonight?
sentences.note: - **sleep over at** one’s **place**: ~ 의 집에서 자다

sentences.text: What’s up? Don’t hold anything back.
sentences.ko: 무슨 일인데? 아무 것도 숨기지 숨기지 마.
sentences.note: - **don’t hold anything back**: 아무 것도 숨기지 않다

sentences.text: We’re having a year-end party overnight.
sentences.note:
- **have a year-end party**: 송년회를 하다
- **overnight**: 밤새도록

sentences.text: I'm terrible with names. What was his name again?
sentences.ko: 내가 이름 외우기에 서투른데. 친구 이름이 뭐라고?
sentences.note: - **be terrible with** sth: ~에 서투르다

sentences.text: Daniel. His parents went on a trip yesterday.
sentences.note: - **go on a trip**: 여행을 가다

sentences.text: OK. I’ll catch a late-night movie with your dad.
sentences.ko: 알았어. 난 네 아빠하고 심야영화나 봐야겠다.

sentences.text: I've had diarrhea for days.
This medication will help you.
I have a slight fever.
I have diarrhea.
I've got the runs.
My neck is stiff.
My eyes are itchy.
I can't stop sneezing.
I have a rash on my arm.
I'm black and blue all over.
I sprained my ankle.
I have trouble swallowing.
My legs fell asleep.
I've got a cramp in my legs.
I have a bug bite.
The economy is worse now more than ever.
sentences.ko: 지금 경기가 그 어느 때보다 더 좋지 않아.
sentences.note: - **more than ever**: 그 어느 때보다 더

sentences.text: The job market is horrible to say the least.
sentences.note: - **to say the least**: 정말로(조금도 과장 없이)

sentences.text: Big companies don’t place many ads to hire people.
sentences.ko: 대기업에서 채용 공고를 많이 내지 않아.
sentences.note: - **place an ad**: 공고(광고)를 내다

sentences.text: Some say we have to lower our standards.
sentences.ko: 어떤 이들은 우리에게 눈높이를 낮추라고 해.
sentences.note: - **lower** one’s **standards**: 눈높이를 낮추다

sentences.text: I think everyone has what it takes to succeed.
sentences.ko: 난 누구나 성공할 자질을 갖추고 있다고 생각해.
sentences.note: - **have what it takes to** V: ~ 할 자질을 갖추고 있다

sentences.text: Let’s face it. It’s too cut-throat these days.
sentences.ko: 현실을 직시하자. 요즘 경쟁이 너무 치열하다고.
sentences.note:
- **Let’s face it**: 현실을 직시하자
- **cut-throat**: 경쟁이 치열한

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게
sentences.text: Are you taking a vacation for Christmas?
sentences.note: - **take a vacation**: 휴가를 내다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게
sentences.text: Yes, I’m going to join a group tour to China.
sentences.note: - **join a group tour** (to 목적지): (~ 로) 단체여행을 가다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게
sentences.text: Good for you! I want to kick back and relax.
sentences.ko: 좋겠어. 나도 긴장을 풀고 푹 쉬고 싶은데.
sentences.note: - **kick back and relax**: 긴장을 풀고 푹 쉬다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게
sentences.text: I need some company. Will you join me?
sentences.note: - **company**: 일행

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게
sentences.text: Sounds tempting. I’ll see if I can clear up my schedule.
sentences.ko: 솔깃한데. 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게.
sentences.note:
- **Sounds tempting**: 솔깃한데
- **clear up** one’s **schedule**: 일정(스케줄)을 비우다

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: 일정을 비울 수 있는지 볼게
sentences.text: You won't be sorry. You have my word.
sentences.note:
- **You won't be sorry**: 후회하지 않을거야
- **You have my word**: 약속해(믿어도 돼)

sentences.text: I sprained my ankle. It really hurts.
Let me take a look. Does this hurt?
I have a terrible headache.
My head is spinning.
My stomach hurts.
I have an upset stomach.
I have a sharp pain in my stomach.
I ache all over.
I can barely move my neck.
I have a bad toothache.
I hurt my back.
My back hurts.
My back is killing me.
It hurts around here.
Did you get good grades in school?
sentences.ko: 학교 다닐 때 좋은 성적을 받았어?
sentences.note: - **get a good grade**: 좋은 성적을 받다

sentences.text: Looking back, I was on the dean’s list during college.
sentences.ko: 돌이켜 보니, 대학 때 우등생 명단에 있었지.
sentences.note:
- **Looking back**: 돌이켜 보니
- **be on the dean’s list**: 우등생 명단에 있다

sentences.text: You were an honor student? Don’t make me laugh.
sentences.note: - **Don’t make me laugh**: 웃기지 마 | 말도 안 돼

sentences.text: OK, but good grades don’t put food on the table.
sentences.ko: 알았어, 하지만 좋은 성적이 밥 먹여주지 않아.
sentences.note: - sth **doesn’t put food on the table**: ~ 가 밥 먹여주지 않는다

sentences.text: There’s nothing like studying hard as a student.
sentences.ko: 학생 때는 공부를 열심히 하는 게 최고야.
sentences.note: - **There’s nothing like** V-ing(N): ~ 만 한 것이 없다 | ~ 가 최고다

sentences.text: I think the point is that I missed the boat in life.
sentences.ko: 핵심은 내가 인생의 (좋은) 기회를 놓쳤다는 거지.
sentences.note:
- **the point is** S V: 요점은 ~ 이다
- **miss the boat**: (좋은) 기회를 놓치다

sentences.text: Time seems to move faster every year.
sentences.ko: 매년 시간이 더 빨리 지나가는 것 같아.
sentences.note: - **move(go by) fast**: (시간이) 빨리 지나가다

sentences.text: We’ve had a lot of ups and downs this year.
sentences.note: - **have a lot of ups and downs**: 수많은 우여곡절을 겪다

sentences.text: Right. I’m having mixed feelings tonight.
sentences.note: - **have mixed feelings** (about sth): (~ 에 대해) 만감이 교차하다 | 여러 감정이 들다

sentences.text: I feel like something is missing at the end of the year.
sentences.ko: 연말에는 뭔가 허전한 것과 같은 기분이 들어.
sentences.note:
- **feel like** S V: ~ 와 같은 기분이 들다
- **something is missing**: 뭔가 허전하다

sentences.text: It’s a bitter-sweet feeling. Let’s make a toast.
sentences.note:
- **bitter-sweet feeling**: 시원섭섭한 감정
- **make a toast** (to sth): (~ 을 위해) 건배하다

sentences.text: Here’s to our friendship and future.
sentences.note: - **Here is to** sth: ~ 을 위하여 건배!

sentences.text: I think I lost my passport.
Let's call the Korean Embassy.
You should visit the Korean Embassy.
Please reissue my passport.
I want to have it reissued.
What do I need to reissue my passport?
I think I lost my wallet.
I left my bag on the train.
I left my wallet in a taxi.
I can't find it anywhere.
Where is the lost and found?
I don't know where I left it.
I'm not sure where I lost it.
I can't remember where I lost it.
I don't remember where I put it.
Let’s go ahead with this plan. We can manage.
sentences.note:
- **go ahead with** sth: ~ 을 추진하다
- sb **can manage**: 그럭저럭 해내다

sentences.text: With your track record, I don’t think we can pull it off.
sentences.ko: 너의 전적을 봤을 때, 우리가 해낼 수 있다고 생각하지 않아.
sentences.note:
- **With** one's **track record**: ~ 의 전적을 봤을 때
- **pull** sth **off**: (어려운 일)을 해내다

sentences.text: Come on! Don’t be such a chicken!
sentences.note: - **Don’t be a chicken!**: 겁먹지 마!

sentences.text: All I’m saying is we need something to turn to.
sentences.ko: 내 말은 뭔가에 의지할 필요가 있다라는 거야.
sentences.note:
- **All I’m saying is** S V: 내 말은 ~ 이라는 거야
- **turn to** sb/sth: ~ 에 의지하다

sentences.text: OK. If you insist, let’s meet halfway.
sentences.note: - **meet** (sb) **halfway**: 절반씩 양보하다

sentences.text: Be serious. It’s no laughing matter.
Happy new year! I hope you make it big next year.
sentences.ko: 새해 복 많이 받아. 내년에 크게 성공하길 바라.
sentences.note: - **make it big**: 크게 성공하다

sentences.text: My family is climbing a mountain to see the sunrise.
sentences.ko: 우리 가족은 일출을 보러 등산을 할거야.
sentences.note:
- **climb a mountain**: 등산을 하다
- **see the sunrise**: 일출을 보다

sentences.text: I guess you will make a wish for the new year.
sentences.note: - **make a wish** (for sth): (~ 을 위해) 소원을 빌다

sentences.text: It’s sort of a ritual at the beginning of the year.
sentences.note:
- **ritual**: 의식(의례)
- **at the beginning of the year**: 연초에

sentences.text: My mother and I will go to get our fortunes told.
sentences.ko: 난 엄마 하고 운세 보러 가려고.
sentences.note: - **get** one’s **fortunes told**: 운세를 보다

sentences.text: Really? You should take it with a grain of salt.
sentences.note: - **take** sth **with a grain of salt**: 걸러서 받아들이다

You should visit the police station.
My bag is missing.
My bag was stolen.
Someone took my bag.
Pickpocket!
I had my pocket picked.
My wallet was taken by a pickpocket.
Please cancel my credit card.
I want to report a theft.
Where should I report it?
Where is the Korean Embassy?
Can you help me find it?
Please call me when you find it.
Where did you find it?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: What's happening to the stock market today?
sentences.ko: 오늘 주식 시장에 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는 건가요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: Oh, well, you wouldn't want to know about this.
sentences.ko: 아, 글쎄요, 알고 싶지 않으실 텐데요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: Not again... But tell me about the damage on my portfolio.
sentences.ko: 또 시작이네요... 그래도 제 포트폴리오의 손실에 대해 말해 주세요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: Overall, you have lost 3%. China became a headache, and you know that you have a couple of China plays.
sentences.ko: 전체적으로 3%의 손실을 보셨습니다. 중국이 골칫거리가 되었는데, 아시다시피 고객님께서 중국 관련주를 두어 개 가지고 계시잖아요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: I didn't know that this would be happening. This is a brand new game.
sentences.ko: 이런 일이 일어날 줄은 몰랐네요. 완전히 새로운 국면이군요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: How was the market today?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: Today the market was pretty weak due to the unexpected China effect.
sentences.ko: 오늘은 예상치 못한 중국 효과 때문에 시장이 꽤 약세였습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: What's the China effect?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: People say that China may increase its interest rate to keep the economy stabilized.
sentences.ko: 중국이 경제 안정을 유지하기 위해 금리를 인상할 수도 있다는 말이 나오고 있습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: This is a brand-new game.
sentences.text: Oh well, this is a whole new ballgame since we have not thought about it before.
sentences.ko: 이런, 전에는 전혀 생각해 보지 않았던 문제라 완전히 새로운 국면이네요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: The market seems to be going nowhere but down over the past two weeks. What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.ko: 지난 2주 동안 시장이 하락세만 보이고 있는 것 같습니다. 시장이 상승하기 위한 기폭제는 무엇이 될까요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: I think the oil price has to come down and stabilize going forward.
sentences.ko: 앞으로 유가가 하락하고 안정되어야 할 것 같습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: I think so, too.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: Unless this oil price situation gets better, our market will be going sideways at best. If not, it's likely to go down further.
sentences.ko: 유가 상황이 나아지지 않는 한, 우리 시장은 기껏해야 횡보세를 보일 것입니다. 그렇지 않다면 더 하락할 가능성이 큽니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: The market has collapsed over the past couple of weeks. What would be a catalyst for the market to move back up?
sentences.ko: 지난 몇 주 동안 시장이 폭락했습니다. 시장이 다시 반등하기 위한 촉매제는 무엇이 될까요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: I reckon the WTI oil price has to come down to $45 or below.
sentences.ko: 제 생각에는 WTI 유가가 45달러 이하로 떨어져야 할 것 같습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: You're absolutely right.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: What would be a catalyst for the market to move up?
sentences.text: Oh well, it seems we're in a situation where we'll have to sink or swim.
sentences.ko: 이런, 우리는 어떻게든 스스로 살아남아야만 하는 상황에 처한 것 같네요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Can I place a buy order?
sentences.text: Hello, Cassie! Things are getting better today. Can I place a buy order?
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 케이시. 오늘은 상황이 좀 나아지고 있네요. 매수 주문을 넣을 수 있을까요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Can I place a buy order?
sentences.text: Sure. What would you like to buy?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Can I place a buy order?

Reflecting these changes, we raise our target price from 320,000 won to 420,000 won, trading at 14.6 times on 17 prospective earnings. Thus, we maintain a Buy stance.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: We need some block trading to get the job done.
sentences.text: Can you give me a reduction in commission rate for a trade for Funds? We also need some block trading to get the job done.
sentences.ko: 펀즈사 거래 건에 대해 수수료율을 좀 인하해 줄 수 있나요? 주문을 완료하려면 블록 트레이딩도 일부 필요합니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: We need some block trading to get the job done.
sentences.text: Sure. We'll charge them only 20 basis points for this particular trade.
sentences.ko: 물론이죠. 이번 특정 거래에 대해서는 20bp(0.2%)만 청구하겠습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: We need some block trading to get the job done.
sentences.text: Thanks. That sounds pretty competitive. Make sure our sales traders find a block sell ASAP.
sentences.ko: 감사합니다. 꽤 경쟁력 있는 조건이네요. 우리 세일즈 트레이더들이 최대한 빨리 블록 매도 물량을 찾도록 해 주세요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: We need some block trading to get the job done.
sentences.text: No worries. We've already got a block of 50,000 shares from Future Asset at that price. And we'll work on the balance in the market until the closing.
sentences.ko: 걱정 마세요. 이미 그 가격에 퓨처에셋으로부터 5만 주의 대량 물량을 확보했습니다. 그리고 남은 잔량은 장 마감 때까지 시장에서 처리하도록 하겠습니다.

sentences.text: Did you know that daily turnover in the KOSPI 200 futures and options market in '04 was down by 11% YoY? The number of futures accounts also decreased from 5,427 to 4,818. Clearly, people are leaving the derivatives market.
sentences.ko: 2004년 코스피 200 선물·옵션 시장의 일평균 거래대금이 전년 대비 11% 감소했다는 사실을 알고 계셨나요? 선물 계좌 수도 5,427개에서 4,818개로 줄어들었습니다. 분명히 사람들이 파생상품 시장을 떠나고 있네요.

sentences.text: From my painful experiences, I've come to the conclusion that 'ignorance is bliss'. As an individual, you cannot make money in the futures and options market. I've heard that small investors are now more interested in indirect investment funds, such as long-term savings-type stock funds.
sentences.ko: 저의 뼈아픈 경험으로 비추어 볼 때, 모르는 게 약이라는 결론에 이르렀어요. 개인으로서 선물·옵션 시장에서 돈을 벌기는 불가능해요. 소액 투자자들은 이제 장기 적립식 주식형 펀드와 같은 간접투자 펀드에 더 관심이 많다고 들었어요.

sentences.text: That's right. Under the current all-time low interest rates, I think this kind of fund is the most suitable for long-term individual investors.
sentences.ko: 맞습니다. 요즘 같은 사상 최저 금리 하에서는 이런 종류의 펀드가 장기 개인 투자자들에게 가장 적합하다고 생각합니다.

sentences.text: Tell me more about this fund, since I need to become more serious about my financial plans this year. My bank account is giving me too little return nowadays.
sentences.ko: 올해는 재무 계획에 대해 좀 더 진지해져야 하니 그 펀드에 대해 더 말씀해 주세요. 요즘 은행 예금은 수익률이 너무 낮아요.

sentences.text: Sure, you put up a small amount of money, say 100,000 won or above, on a monthly basis for 1 to 3 years. It reduces the time risk by spreading out the purchasing times. Since this is an accumulated fund, you wouldn't miss a big rally in the stock market. Thus, I don't normally ask people to invest in the stock market, but this is a no-brainer.
sentences.ko: 그러죠, 1년에서 3년 동안 매달 10만 원 이상의 소액을 적립하는 방식입니다. 매수 시점을 분산시킴으로써 시간적 위험을 줄여줍니다. 적립식 펀드이기 때문에 주식 시장의 큰 상승세를 놓치지 않을 수 있습니다. 따라서 저는 평소에 사람들에게 주식 투자를 권하지 않지만, 이것은 생각할 필요도 없이 명백히 좋은 선택입니다.

sentences.text: It sounds perfect for me. I'll drop by to invest in this fund right away.
sentences.ko: 저에게 딱 맞는 것 같네요. 당장 그 펀드에 가입하러 들를게요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: You don't have to hit a home run from day one.
sentences.text: (On the phone) Amy, how are things with you in London?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: You don't have to hit a home run from day one.
sentences.text: Things are great here, boss. Since I'm working in the center of the financial world in Europe, I feel responsible for bringing more clients to generate business.
sentences.ko: 여기 생활은 아주 좋습니다, 부장님. 유럽 금융의 중심지에서 일하고 있는 만큼, 사업을 창출하기 위해 더 많은 고객을 유치해야 한다는 책임감을 느껴요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: You don't have to hit a home run from day one.
sentences.text: Look Amy, you don't have to hit a home run from day one. Just get up to speed on what's going on around there, and put first things first.
sentences.ko: 에이미, 첫날부터 홈런을 칠 필요는 없어요. 그곳에서 무슨 일이 일어나고 있는지 파악하고, 중요한 일부터 먼저 처리하세요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: You don't have to hit a home run from day one.
sentences.text: That is one of the issues I need to address. Last year, the London financial industry posted a net export of 17 billion pounds, which was the record high, and the trend continues into this year. Also, 70% of European hedge funds, or 154 billion pounds, is now invested through London. Its forex market turnover is the largest with 36% market share, exceeding the US's 21% and Japan's 6%.
sentences.ko: 그것이 바로 제가 다루어야 할 문제 중 하나입니다. 작년에 런던 금융업은 사상 최고치인 170억 파운드의 순수출을 기록했고, 그 추세는 올해도 이어지고 있습니다. 또한 유럽 헤지펀드의 70%인 1,540억 파운드가 현재 런던을 통해 투자되고 있습니다. 외환 시장 거래액은 시장 점유율 36%로 가장 크며, 미국의 21%와 일본의 6%를 앞서고 있습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: You don't have to hit a home run from day one.
sentences.text: What made the London financial market grow like that?
sentences.ko: 무엇이 런던 금융 시장을 그렇게 성장하게 만들었나요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: You don't have to hit a home run from day one.
sentences.text: If you bring your money to London today, you can run your business from the next day. You wouldn't believe how efficiently the financial infrastructure operates here. The British people set up big principles based on practices which have been used over the last 300 years, and they do everything by principle.
sentences.ko: 오늘 런던으로 자금을 가져오면 다음 날부터 바로 사업을 운영할 수 있습니다. 이곳의 금융 인프라가 얼마나 효율적으로 운영되는지 믿기 어려우실 겁니다. 영국인들은 지난 300년 동안 사용되어 온 관행을 바탕으로 대원칙을 세웠으며, 모든 일을 원칙에 따라 처리합니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Have you received my executions?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Sure, but your executions are not impressive! What happened to your buy-low, sell-high rule of thumb?
sentences.ko: 네, 하지만 체결 결과가 별로 인상적이지 않네요! 당신의 저가 매수, 고가 매도 원칙은 어떻게 된 겁니까?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Sorry about that. I must have been doing the other way around. I'll promise to make it up next time.
sentences.ko: 죄송합니다. 제가 반대로 매매했나 봅니다. 다음번에는 꼭 만회하도록 하겠습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Oh, well. Who says that there would be a next time?
sentences.ko: 글쎄요. 다음 기회가 또 있을지 누가 압니까?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: My dealer told me that the Hyundai Motor trade was really bad.
sentences.ko: 저희 딜러가 현대차 매매 체결 결과가 아주 나빴다고 하더군요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Yes, I must admit that we did not beat VWAP. Market was moving up and down against us, but still it's all our fault. No cheap excuses.
sentences.ko: 네, 저희가 거래량가중평균가(VWAP)보다 좋은 가격에 체결하지 못했음을 인정합니다. 시장이 저희에게 불리한 방향으로 요동쳤지만, 그래도 전적으로 저희 잘못입니다. 구차한 변명은 하지 않겠습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Oh, well. That's fine. It can be a mere judgment matter.
sentences.ko: 아, 괜찮습니다. 그저 판단의 문제일 수도 있으니까요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: Your executions are not impressive!
sentences.text: Thanks a lot. We'll do our best next time.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: It has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.text: Hello, this is the Unfair Practice Supervisory Unit of the FSC. Can I speak to the branch manager? We need to ask him to submit a report.
sentences.ko: 여보세요, 금융위원회 불공정거래 조사팀입니다. 지점장님과 통화할 수 있을까요? 보고서 제출을 요청해야 합니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: It has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.text: Yes, this is the branch manager. What can I do for you?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: It has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.text: Oh, well, we've got a complaint from the Korean Stock Exchange that some accounts in your branch may be involved with stock price manipulation for a couple of small-cap companies.
sentences.ko: 아, 네, 귀 지점의 일부 계좌가 몇몇 소형주의 시세조종(주가조작)에 연루되었을 가능성이 있다는 민원이 한국거래소로부터 접수되었습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: It has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.text: I see. There must be a misunderstanding here, because we have our own internal control system, this should not happen. However, I will investigate the case immediately.
sentences.ko: 그렇군요. 저희 자체 내부통제 시스템이 있어서 이런 일이 일어날 리 없으니, 분명 오해가 있었을 것입니다. 하지만, 즉각 해당 건을 조사해 보겠습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: It has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.text: Within the next 3 days, please send a report for all the trades done with these accounts for the last 6 months.
sentences.ko: 앞으로 3일 이내에 해당 계좌들로 지난 6개월 동안 이루어진 모든 거래에 대한 보고서를 보내주십시오.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: It has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.text: Yes, sir. I will ask my back-office people to send the report by then. I hope it has nothing to do with any unfair practice.
sentences.ko: 알겠습니다. 그때까지 보고서를 보내도록 후선 부서(업무지원팀) 직원들에게 요청하겠습니다. 어떠한 불공정 행위와도 무관하기를 바랍니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Where are institutional investors in our market?
sentences.text: Breeze, word's spreading like wildfire that you've been selected as the best fund manager of the year at Funds.
sentences.ko: 브리즈, 네가 Funds 사에서 올해의 최우수 펀드매니저로 선정되었다는 소문이 삽시간에 퍼지고 있어.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Where are institutional investors in our market?
sentences.text: I'm just doing fine, James. No big deal. How are you this afternoon?
sentences.ko: 그저 잘하고 있을 뿐이야, 제임스. 대단한 일도 아닌걸. 오늘 오후는 어때?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Where are institutional investors in our market?
sentences.text: Couldn't be better. Concerning your question on how much SEC you should have in your portfolio, you should maintain the current weighting of 22% even though the market cap weighting has fallen down to 18%. I believe SEC will outperform the market soon, and then you can do better than your competitors, who normally have the market weighting of only 18%.
sentences.ko: 더할 나위 없이 좋아. 네 포트폴리오에 SEC 비중을 얼마나 두어야 하는지에 대한 질문에 대해서는, 비록 시가총액 비중이 18%까지 떨어졌지만 현재의 22% 비중을 유지해야 해. 나는 SEC가 조만간 시장 수익률을 상회할 것이라 믿고, 그러면 보통 18% 정도의 시장 비중만 보유하고 있는 경쟁자들보다 더 나은 성과를 낼 수 있을 거야.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Where are institutional investors in our market?
sentences.text: Sounds like a winning strategy for me. Besides, I want to maintain a longer term investment horizon as an institutional investor. Thus, I don't want to reduce it.
sentences.ko: 나에게 승산이 있는 전략인 것 같네. 게다가 기관투자자로서 나는 좀 더 장기적인 투자 시계를 유지하고 싶어. 따라서 비중을 줄이고 싶지 않아.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Where are institutional investors in our market?
sentences.text: Actually, I keep asking myself, "Where are institutional investors in our market?" Currently, the weighting of institutional investors is slightly over 17%, compared with 31% at the end of 1996, right before the IMF crisis. This is also way below as opposed to the US's 47% or Japan's 21%.
sentences.ko: 사실, 우리 시장에서 기관투자자들은 다 어디로 갔는지 스스로에게 계속 묻게 돼. 현재 기관투자자 비중은 IMF 외환위기 직전인 1996년 말의 31%와 비교해 겨우 17%를 조금 넘는 수준이야. 이는 미국의 47%나 일본의 21%에 비해서도 훨씬 낮은 수치지.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 3: Where are institutional investors in our market?
sentences.text: Our government has to accelerate public funds' investment into equities.
sentences.ko: 우리 정부는 공적 자금의 주식 투자를 촉진해야 해.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: Hello, may I speak to Ms. Sophie Park in the operations department?
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 업무부의 소피 박 씨와 통화할 수 있을까요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: Sure. Hold on a minute. I'll put you through.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: Good morning, Securities One, Sophie speaking.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: This is Mr. Foong calling from Funds. I just wonder if you can help me on this matter.
sentences.ko: 펀즈 사의 펑입니다. 이 건에 관해 도움을 받을 수 있을까 해서요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: Hi, Mr. Foong. I hope I can help you. What is it?
sentences.ko: 안녕하세요, 펑 씨. 도움이 되어 드릴 수 있으면 좋겠네요. 어떤 일인가요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number? I need to open an institutional account for the Hong Kong Country Club.
sentences.ko: 외국인 투자등록번호(ID)를 발급받는 데 얼마나 걸리나요? 홍콩 컨트리 클럽의 기관 계좌를 개설해야 해서요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: Mr. Foong, that's an easy one since I am the one who handles that matter. It takes about three or four days if you apply for it either on Tuesday or Thursday. Otherwise, it takes a week.
sentences.ko: 펑 씨, 제가 그 업무를 담당하고 있어서 쉽게 처리해 드릴 수 있습니다. 화요일이나 목요일에 신청하시면 3~4일 정도 걸립니다. 그렇지 않으면 일주일 정도 소요됩니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: Oh, that's quite specific. Thank you very much for your help. I'll get someone to send the necessary documents to you later.
sentences.ko: 아, 아주 구체적이네요. 도와주셔서 정말 감사합니다. 필요한 서류들을 나중에 사람을 시켜 보내드리도록 하겠습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 1: How long does it take to obtain a foreign ID number?
sentences.text: It's my pleasure, and I'll wait for the materials. Have a good day.
sentences.ko: 천만에요, 자료 기다리고 있겠습니다. 좋은 하루 보내세요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: SK E&S has managed to issue a 3-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history.
sentences.text: This is practically day one for me. How would you like to be addressed?
sentences.ko: 저는 사실상 오늘이 첫 출근일입니다. 어떻게 불러드리면 될까요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: SK E&S has managed to issue a 3-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history.
sentences.text: Please just call me DJ. By the way, you look familiar.
sentences.ko: 그냥 DJ라고 불러주세요. 그런데, 낯이 많이 익으시네요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: SK E&S has managed to issue a 3-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history.
sentences.text: I think I've seen you somewhere in the past. It's such a coincidence meeting you here.
sentences.ko: 전에 어디선가 뵌 적이 있는 것 같아요. 여기서 이렇게 만나다니 정말 우연이네요.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: SK E&S has managed to issue a 3-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history.
sentences.text: Anyway, I've heard a lot about you. Welcome to our department. We've been busy lately with a new fixed income issue for SK E&S, which is a city gas provider among SK affiliates.
sentences.ko: 어쨌든, 말씀 많이 들었습니다. 저희 부서에 오신 것을 환영합니다. 최근 저희는 SK 계열 도시가스 공급사인 SK E&S의 신규 채권 발행 건으로 바빴습니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: SK E&S has managed to issue a 3-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history.
sentences.text: Yes, I've heard of it. SK E&S has managed to issue a three-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history. It couldn't be better than this!
sentences.ko: 네, 이야기 들었습니다. SK E&S가 역사상 최저 금리로 3년 만기 회사채를 발행하는 데 성공했더군요. 이보다 더 좋을 수는 없죠!

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: SK E&S has managed to issue a 3-year corporate bond at the lowest rate in history.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: Can a private equity fund increase corporate values?
sentences.text: Since the PEF Act was passed in September 2004, there have been many discussions about PEF. Can a private equity fund increase corporate values?
sentences.ko: 2004년 9월에 사모펀드법이 통과된 이후, 사모펀드에 관한 많은 논의가 있어 왔습니다. 사모투자펀드가 기업 가치를 높일 수 있나요?

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: Can a private equity fund increase corporate values?
sentences.text: Yes. Unlike M&A funds which seek only capital gains, PEF makes an all-out effort to increase corporate value for the invested company. That's why it's described as "capitalism's new king" by the Economist. This journal mentions that the following products held the foremost positions for the needs of the times: Junk bonds represented by Michael Milken in the '80s, the U.S. treasury bonds in the early '90s, IBs in the late '90s, and then PEFs represented by Blackstone, Carlyle, and KKR in the 2000s.
sentences.ko: 네. 단순 매매차익만을 노리는 M&A 펀드와 달리, 사모펀드는 투자한 기업의 기업 가치를 높이기 위해 전방위적인 노력을 기울입니다. 그것이 이코노미스트지에서 사모펀드를 '자본주의의 새로운 제왕'으로 묘사한 이유입니다. 이 저널은 시대적 요구에 따라 다음과 같은 금융 상품들이 선도적 위치를 차지했다고 언급합니다. 80년대에는 마이클 밀켄으로 대표되는 정크 본드, 90년대 초에는 미국 국채, 90년대 후반에는 투자은행(IB), 그리고 2000년대에는 블랙스톤, 칼라일, KKR로 대표되는 사모투자펀드(PEF)입니다.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: Can a private equity fund increase corporate values?
sentences.text: Actually, Korea neglected introducing this new type of capital raising. That's why so many troubled banks have been bought by foreign PEFs over the past few years, while domestic players' hands were completely tied up.

sentences.paragraph_title: Paragraph 2: Can a private equity fund increase corporate values?
sentences.text: Yes. Newbridge took over KFB, Lone Star took over KEB, and Carlyle took over KorAm Bank. And all of them have managed to make astronomical gains by selling back their stakes in these banks, while Korean firms haven't been allowed to set up PEFs due to the misconception that PEFs could be manipulated by the existing Chaebuls.
sentences.ko: 맞습니다. 뉴브리지는 제일은행(KFB)을 인수했고, 론스타는 외환은행(KEB)을, 칼라일은 한미은행을 인수했습니다. 그리고 그들 모두 이 은행들의 지분을 재매각하여 천문학적인 수익을 올렸지만, 한국 기업들은 사모펀드가 기존 재벌들에 의해 악용될 수 있다는 오해 때문에 사모펀드 설립이 허용되지 않았습니다.
